For those unaware of how the All-MLB team gets selected, this is the description from the press release: Fans and panelists will vote for their choices at catcher, first base, second base, third base, shortstop, three outfielders (without regard for left/center/right) and designated hit
item.content:encoded:
Two Mets are on the ballot for the 2026 'All-MLB' team, Juan Soto and Nolan McLean. Voting opens today and runs through Friday, October 9. The team will be announced at the MLB Awards on November 11 in Las Vegas. For those unaware of how the All-MLB team gets selected, this is the description from the press release:
Fans and panelists will vote for their choices at catcher, first base, second base, third base, shortstop, three outfielders (without regard for left/center/right) and designated hitter, along with five starting pitchers and two relief pitchers on both the first and second teams. All choices will be based on the 2026 regular season, without regard for American League or National League affiliation.
McLean, a Rookie of the Year contender, put up 3.0 bWAR in his first full season alongside a 3.16 ERA, 128 ERA+, 194 strikeouts in 179 and two-thirds innings, while making 31 starts. Soto, who missed 51 games due to injury, also put up 3.0 bWAR while hitting .275/.393/.515 with 27 home runs and a 154 OPS+.
Other outfield selections include Pete Crow-Armstrong, Mike Trout, James Wood, and Byron Buxton. Other starting pitcher nominees include Sandy Alcantara, Jacob deGrom, Zack Wheeler, and Tarik Skubal.
The full list of nominees can be found here, and you can vote here.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] David Stearns addresses possible regrets over Pete Alonso situation: ‘I don’t get mulligans’
item.dc:creator: John Flanigan
item.description: David Stearns didn't speak when Pete Alonso was in to town with the Orioles. So sitting in the Citi Field press conference room just two weeks later, the Mets' president of baseball operations was asked if he had any regrets over the way things went down. Alonso, of course, left the Mets this offseason for a big money five-year deal with the Orioles after not receiving an offer from the only organization he'd ever known. In turn, Stearns attempted to replace his production by bringing in veteran
item.content:encoded:
David Stearns didn't speak when Pete Alonso was in to town with the Orioles.
So sitting in the Citi Field press conference room just two weeks later, the Mets' president of baseball operations was asked if he had any regrets over the way things went down.
Alonso, of course, left the Mets this offseason for a big money five-year deal with the Orioles after not receiving an offer from the only organization he'd ever known.
In turn, Stearns attempted to replace his production by bringing in veteran Jorge Polanco, who ended up appearing in just 37 games after battling wrist and ankle injuries.
So after seeing Mets fans give their fan favorite ovation after ovation in his heroic Citi Field return, Stearns said it's a fair question looking back on things.
"The truth is in this job I don't get mulligans," he emphasized. "I also recognize Pete had a tremendous year, and the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough, so my job now is to ensure that we've got better success across our roster, but for the entirety of the season better production at first base, as well."
Alonso showed no ill-effects transitioning during his first year in the American League, as he became the first player in baseball history to lead both leagues in RBI in separate seasons (113).
He also launched a league-high 43 homers and posted career-best marks in OBP (.363) and OPS (.884), among several other offensive statistics, while missing just one game (Sunday's rainout in the Bronx).
The Mets, on the other hand, struggled to receive much of anything from the position before Jared Young stepped up with his breakout second-half of the season.
Even with Young's production, it wasn't nearly good enough.
"I give Pete an enormous amount of credit, he went out and had a great year," Stearns said. "Our entire season our first base production wasn't neatly good enough, now it's my job to put a group together that plays better."

item.title: [heavy.com] Mets' Bo Bichette Arrives at $42 Million Decision
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The New York Mets dished out a huge free agent contract to Bo Bichette in an effort to pursue a World Series title. These Mets, though, weren’t even close to making the playoffs in Bichette’s first season in town. It works out to be quite the disappointment for all involved. Bichette had just played in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series with his Toronto Blue Jays. The Mets had just missed the playoffs with a brutal collapse in the season’s final week. Both were looking to take a step forward, and t
item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets dished out a huge free agent contract to Bo Bichette in an effort to pursue a World Series title.
These Mets, though, weren’t even close to making the playoffs in Bichette’s first season in town.
It works out to be quite the disappointment for all involved.
Bichette had just played in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series with his Toronto Blue Jays.
The Mets had just missed the playoffs with a brutal collapse in the season’s final week.
Both were looking to take a step forward, and the Mets had the money to lure Bichette away from Toronto and try to achieve greatness.
Their first year together left a lot to be desired, though, and now it’s a question whether there’ll be more.
Bo Bichette Contract
When Bichette signed with the Mets, his contract was described as a three-year deal worth $126 million — which is $42 million per year.
But as the details came out, it was noted that the contract wasn’t just a three-year pact. It was layered with opt-outs.
Bichette is able to opt-out after the 2026 season if he wants. He can also opt-out after 2027 if he wants.
The contract essentially functions as three one-year deals put together. If Bichette rides out the life of the contract, he gets $126 million.
But each season is its own $42 million, and Bichette was given the chance to leave between each one with his player options.
If Bichette played up to his potential in 2026, he’d be an obvious opt-out candidate to go to free agency again and get an even larger contract.
But after a so-so Bichette season, and with a potential lockout incoming, Bichette may decide to stay put. It’ll be a fascinating decision-making process to watch.
Bo Bichette Season Stats
Bichette started the year incredibly cold, which is important context to note when looking at some of Bichette’s stats.
He batted .260, which was the second-worst average season of his career. His .702 OPS was also second-worst of Bichette’s career.
He was available almost every day (160 games) while playing a new spot, third base.
Bichette hit 25 doubles, two triples and 18 home runs. He drove in 78 runs and scored 76 runs.
It wasn’t a bad season, per se, but for a guy who twice led the American League in hits, it was a disappointing one.
The Mets and their owner, Steve Cohen, have plenty of money, so they won’t regret this signing. It was a logical one.
But they likely are watching closely to what Bichette does with 2027 player option on his contract. There’s a world where not paying Bichette $42 million next season could work out better for the Mets.
The potentially disjointed offseason could make everything a bit weirder here, too, but keep an eye on Bichette. One way or another, he’s got a decision to make.

item.title: [sportingnews.com] Orioles' Pete Alonso makes RBI MLB history that surprisingly hasn't happened before | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles didn't have a great 2026 season, but the presence of Pete Alonso provided a spark worth getting excited about moving forward. He led the American League in home runs and put up a 4.9 bWAR season, the best season he's had since his 2019 rookie year with the New York Mets. But Alonso has made MLB history with a different season during his Mets tenure. Sarah Langs shared that Alonso is the first hitter in MLB history since 1920 to lead the American League and the National Leag
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Orioles didn't have a great 2026 season, but the presence of Pete Alonso provided a spark worth getting excited about moving forward.
He led the American League in home runs and put up a 4.9 bWAR season, the best season he's had since his 2019 rookie year with the New York Mets. But Alonso has made MLB history with a different season during his Mets tenure.
Sarah Langs shared that Alonso is the first hitter in MLB history since 1920 to lead the American League and the National League in RBIs, as he led the NL in RBIs in 2022 and the AL in 2026.
Pete Alonso made MLB history that surprisingly hasn't happened before
"Pete Alonso led the AL in RBI. He led the NL (and tied for the MLB lead) in 2022. He's the first player to have a season leading each league in RBI in his career (RBI since 1920)," Langs shared.
In 2026 with the Orioles, Alonso has 113 RBIs, which is the most in the American League, although it's not the most in Major League Baseball.
Back in 2022, Alonso had 131 RBIs, the most in the NL and all of MLB that season. Combined with his 2026 production, Alonso has become the first player to finish a season as the league leader in the AL and NL in RBIs.
This is an unexpected MLB record for Alonso, as it's a bit surprising that no other player was ever able to accomplish this fairly straightforward feat.
While players weren't changing teams back then as much as they do now, it's still unexpected that this has never happened before.
But this is still a very impressive feat for Alonso, as he's now the only player to lead both the AL and NL in RBIs in a single season.
He's also led the AL and NL in home runs, hitting 53 homers in his rookie season to lead all of MLB, and hitting 43 homers in 2026 to lead the AL, two behind Pete Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead.
This statistic highlights how great Alonso has been for the Orioles, as the new first baseman has become a massive piece of the Orioles' franchise and should be the focal point moving forward for a new era of Orioles baseball.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Vinnie Pasquantino Has a Clear Message for the Royals After a Disappointing 2026
item.dc:creator: David Martinez
item.description: Vinnie Pasquantino had one last chance to give Kansas City Royals fans something to feel good about before the offseason began, and he made the most of it Sunday afternoon. Two home runs, a 3-2 win over Cleveland and a little water celebration to close out the season at Kauffman Stadium. For Pasquantino, though, the most revealing part of the afternoon came when he was asked what he expects from Kansas City moving forward. The first baseman wasn't interested in making promises about what next se
item.content:encoded:
Vinnie Pasquantino had one last chance to give Kansas City Royals fans something to feel good about before the offseason began, and he made the most of it Sunday afternoon.
Two home runs, a 3-2 win over Cleveland and a little water celebration to close out the season at Kauffman Stadium. For Pasquantino, though, the most revealing part of the afternoon came when he was asked what he expects from Kansas City moving forward.
The first baseman wasn't interested in making promises about what next season will look like. He's been down that road before.
"I think the optimism is I know what work we're going to do this offseason, just as individuals of trying to get better," Pasquantino told Royals TV's Bridget Howard after the finale. "So we try not to make too many proclamations. I did that when I was a little bit younger and learned from it."
That answer says plenty about where the Royals are after a 69-93 season that fell well short of the expectations they carried into April. Kansas City had hoped to build on its back-to-back winning seasons, but instead finished last in the AL Central and now faces an offseason of questions about how to get back to the postseason.
Pasquantino wasn't interested in dressing that up, either.
"When we don't make it, we look at it as a failure, and that's what this was," he said.
It was an unusually direct assessment from a player who has spent much of the season trying to get his own production back on track. Pasquantino finished with a .249 average and 17 home runs in 114 games, numbers that reflect a difficult year interrupted by injuries and stretches of inconsistent hitting.
Sunday offered a much better ending. Pasquantino twice gave Kansas City the lead with solo shots off Cleveland's Austin Peterson, including a go-ahead homer in the eighth inning. It was his first career multi-homer game at Kauffman Stadium and his eighth home run in 23 September games.
Asked about finishing healthy, Pasquantino made clear that was more important to him than the final numbers.
"It's not about chasing results. It's just chasing good at-bats, chasing good swings," he said postgame.
That approach may be particularly relevant for a team that will need its established hitters to rebound next season. Pasquantino also pointed to the progress of Carter Jensen and Jac Caglianone, calling their contributions a major success from the season and saying there's more to come from Caglianone.
The young core gives Kansas City something to build around, but Pasquantino knows development alone won't erase what happened in 2026.
"I'm walking into next season expecting us to be in a playoff push the whole year," he told MLB.com's Jackson Stone. "Those are just words; they don't mean anything right now, but those are my expectations. We just gotta go do it."
For Pasquantino, the offseason begins with the same responsibility he believes every Royal has: looking in the mirror and figuring out how to make the next season different.

item.title: [MLB.com] Crochet has chance to make Red Sox's Wild Card Series roster as reliever
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne
item.description: NEW YORK -- Who could forget the tone that Garrett Crochet set at Yankee Stadium in Game 1 of last year’s American League Wild Card Series, when he turned in a masterful performance which included 11 strikeouts over 7 2/3 innings and 117 pitches? But the fact that Crochet’s even here, and in very much in play to be added to the roster as a reliever when it is announced on Tuesday, is satisfying to the lefty who finished second in the AL Cy Young Award race last season. This season was a rough le
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Who could forget the tone that Garrett Crochet set at Yankee Stadium in Game 1 of last year’s American League Wild Card Series, when he turned in a masterful performance which included 11 strikeouts over 7 2/3 innings and 117 pitches?
But the fact that Crochet’s even here, and in very much in play to be added to the roster as a reliever when it is announced on Tuesday, is satisfying to the lefty who finished second in the AL Cy Young Award race last season.
This season was a rough letdown, filled with left shoulder woes, a setback, and ultimately months of strengthening and rehabbing the capsule that surrounds his rotator cuff just so he could be cleared to throw again.
On Saturday, in Fort Myers, Fla., he threw his second live batting practice session of the week.
“It was good. Been feeling good. I guess now it's just a matter if anybody agrees with me,” said Crochet.
“We're still seeing,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “Again, like I said, he threw the live BP and came out of it well. We'll see as we get to the end of the workout if we can key down on making decisions like that.”
One key question is if Crochet will be able to pitch more than once against the Yankees, which feels important in a best-of-three format.
“I think the answer to that is up in the air,” said Tracy. “If we're able to activate Garrett and we do that and we decide to do that, obviously he's available, right? I think beyond that, if you were to use him, the availability, whether that's the next day or for another game in the Series, it's still going to be contingent on us continuing to evaluate him.
“We know where he's at. We know he's worked very hard to get everything back strong the way it needs to be, but we're still going to be evaluating him daily to see where he's at. Whether he's available to pitch [more than once] in this series, I don't know the answer to that yet.”
For months, Crochet was frustrated by a rehab that turned out to be longer than he ever envisioned. But he didn’t let that frustration diminish his motivation to put himself in position to be part of Boston’s playoff run.
“It was obviously a lot longer than I expected. Been busting my tail just to kind of give myself a fighting chance, and I feel like I did that,” said Crochet. “Now it's just waiting for the roster to come out. I hope that I'm able to contribute, but regardless, I'm here, and I think that we have put ourselves in a great position to walk away from the Series with a win.”
Last year, Crochet got the only win of the series for the Red Sox. This year, Boston looks for a chance to get rivalry redemption.
Will that experience in Game 1 last year help him if he gets the chance to face the Yankees again this week?
“It's more so just awareness of being in the moment of the postseason and being able to quiet the noise on the outside, just not letting the moment get too big,” Crochet said.
Pitching in relief is familiar for Crochet. He did it in college at Tennessee and in his first 72 career appearances (2.71 ERA) for the White Sox before he was converted to a starting pitcher in ‘24.
Considering that Crochet hasn’t had time to stretch out his pitch count, one or two-inning stints seem most likely should he make the roster.

item.title: [MLB.com] Fresh off facial fractures, Bregman mashes 2 homers in 2nd game back
item.dc:creator: Jordan Bastian
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG – Even without any postseason implications on the line on Sunday, Alex Bregman told Cubs manager Craig Counsell that he wanted to be in the starting lineup. The third baseman felt it was important for him to get more at-bats ahead of the playoffs. And if there were any lingering questions about how Bregman was seeing the ball just a week removed from the fluke foul ball that resulted in multiple fractures in his left cheek, he offered an emphatic answer against the Red Sox. In onl
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG – Even without any postseason implications on the line on Sunday, Alex Bregman told Cubs manager Craig Counsell that he wanted to be in the starting lineup. The third baseman felt it was important for him to get more at-bats ahead of the playoffs.
And if there were any lingering questions about how Bregman was seeing the ball just a week removed from the fluke foul ball that resulted in multiple fractures in his left cheek, he offered an emphatic answer against the Red Sox. In only his second game back in the lineup, Bregman belted a pair of no-doubt homers in his first two at-bats at Tropicana Field.
Following two games on Friday at Fenway Park, where strong winds related to the Nor’easter hitting the region did a number on Chicago’s offense, the move to the neutral site gave the lineup a chance to hit reset. That was especially important for Bregman, who went 0-for-4 in his first game back in the opener of Friday’s twin bill.
Late Saturday night, Bregman went over video with Ben Martin, an assistant director of Major League development for the Cubs, at the team’s hotel. They found some issues with Bregman’s posture in his stance during Friday’s at-bats and went to work on correcting the issue. And on Sunday afternoon, Counsell received a text message from the third baseman.
“It just said, ‘LFG,’” Counsell said with a smirk. “I knew what it meant – I didn’t know what he was referring to. I thought he was referring to a football game or something like that. But he was like, ‘I found it and I’m ready. I feel good.’ And yeah, he did. He felt good. He was right.”
Bregman cracked a smile when asked about the text.
“[We were] trying to figure out what felt a little weird the first game back,” Bregman said. “I was kind of looking uphill and kind of [leaning] back. So I kind of got a little bit more into it, into a little bit more of an attacking posture today. It felt better.”
That is great news ahead of the upcoming National League Wild Card Series against the Padres.
“I’m not surprised that he’s performing when he’s back on the field,” Counsell said. “I’m surprised that he’s back on the field. Being back on the field is what I think we should all appreciate and admire.”
The only question right now is whether Counsell will put Bregman back at third base in the postseason, or keep him slotted in as the designated hitter for now. Bregman has been the DH in his first two games back in the fold, and Counsell hinted at staying in that mode as a way to minimize the risk of a setback.
Bregman took ground balls in a workout at Tropicana Field on Saturday’s off-day and will do so again during Monday’s workout at Petco Park in San Diego. Even so, Counsell is taking things day by day when it comes to weighing putting him back in the field.
“We’ll just kind of see how he feels every day,” Counsell said. “I think he’s improving every day, but he’s got multiple face fractures, and it’s been [a week]. So we’ll just see how he feels. One thing I’m thinking about is the risk of more exposure. I think his at-bats are the most important thing that we can get.”
Bregman said he is willing to do whatever Counsell asks of him.
“I want to play third, but I’ll do whatever it takes,” Bregman said.
Bregman went deep in the first and third inning – off a first-pitch sinker and then an 0-1 sweeper – and sent both pitches crashing into the left-field stands. Those were the 27th and 28th homers of the year for Bregman, who has been one of baseball’s best hitters in the second half. Entering the final game of the regular season, only Pete Crow-Armstrong (4.7), Fernando Tatis Jr. (3.7) and Elly De La Cruz (3.6) had a higher WAR (via FanGraphs) than Bregman (3.3) since the All-Star break.
Bregman added a single in the fifth inning, drew a walk in the seventh and added an RBI double in the ninth. When he reached base after those plate appearances, Bregman switched out one helmet (with an extended left earflap) for another that had a longer flap on each side to offer more protection.
“I felt like I was in a football helmet out there,” Bregman quipped.
Bregman was waiting on deck on Sept. 20 in Cincinnati when he was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch. Prior to that game, the Cubs’ third baseman had hit .298 with 19 homers, 18 doubles, 53 RBIs and a 1.000 OPS in his previous 60 games. His season OPS climbed to .801 from .670 in that span.
Beyond the homers, Bregman ended the year slashing .265/.355/.464 with 33 doubles, 76 walks, 92 runs scored, 93 RBIs and an .819 OPS in 155 games for the North Siders.
“The last two months of the season, I feel like that’s who I am as a player,” Bregman said. “I’m proud to know that no matter how big of a hole that I dug myself, I could find my way back out.”

item.title: [MLB.com] After playing most games in a decade, Trout 'excited' for what's next
item.dc:creator: Rhett Bollinger

The Angels previously were the only current franchise never to top the century mark in losses. The 35-year-old played in 142 games, including 109 games in center field, his most action there since ’22. Trout credited
item.content:encoded:
SEATTLE -- After playing in his most games in a season since 2016, Angels superstar Mike Trout was held out of the lineup for Sunday’s season finale against the Mariners, which saw the club reach 100 losses for the first time in franchise history with a 7-3 defeat at T-Mobile Park. The Angels previously were the only current franchise never to top the century mark in losses.
The 35-year-old played in 142 games, including 109 games in center field, his most action there since ’22. Trout credited the training staff, strength staff and his personal physical therapist for keeping him on the field. His only injury was a right hamstring strain in mid-June that forced him to miss 17 games.
“It means a lot,” Trout said ahead of the Angels' 7-3 loss. “Going into the offseason last year, just coming up with a plan and sticking to it. I'm proud of myself to be able to stick with it. I had a little hiccup in Arizona for a couple weeks. But being out there with the guys and getting the confidence that I can be out there every day, it means a lot to me.”
Trout, a three-time AL MVP and 12-time All-Star, batted .242/.382/.421 with 22 homers, 26 doubles, 11 stolen bases, 86 runs and 54 RBIs in 142 games. His .803 OPS was a drop from his career .963 OPS and Trout said there were times he felt like he was pressing and trying to find his mechanics, especially in the middle of the season.
“Started off great,” Trout said. “After the All-Star break, I battled through some stuff. When I'm right at the plate, I feel like I can still be the MVP like I used to be. You guys have seen it, like in the New York series. I felt like that the whole year when I was winning the MVPs. So just trying to stick to that.”
Trout also expressed gratitude to manager Kurt Suzuki for allowing him to return to his natural position in center field after a move to right field in ’25. Among advanced metrics, his range was below average with -5 Outs Above Average (OAA), but he displayed an above-average arm and still ranks in the 83rd percentile in sprint speed.
“I want to thank Zuk for just trusting me to go out there and play the position I played my whole life,” Trout said. “We had great communication the whole year on how I felt. And like I said, just appreciate Zuk just sticking with it.”
Trout praised Suzuki for his communication skills and said his teammates like playing for him. But Suzuki is on a one-year deal and his future remains unclear. Suzuki said he didn’t have an update on his status, but the Angels could make an announcement as soon as Monday.
“I wish I could tell you guys,” Suzuki said. “Honestly, there's nothing happening right now. Obviously, things can change in the next 24 hours, but as of right now, it's still kind of status quo."
The Angels are in a transition period with Stan Kroenke agreeing to purchase the club from Arte Moreno on Sept. 1. The transaction is expected to become official in early 2027, which could play into whether interim general manager John Mozeliak remains in his role and if Suzuki returns in ’27.
Trout said he’s already had conversations from people at Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE), but not Kroenke just yet. But he’s excited about the future, because all of Kroenke's teams in major sports have won titles in recent years: the NFL’s LA Rams, the NBA’s Denver Nuggets, the NHL’s Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal in the English Premier League.
“It's super exciting,” Trout said. “The conversations that we had, I'm obviously going to keep it in-house but it was very positive. And it gets me excited.”
Trout remains under contract through 2030 after signing a 12-year, $426.5 million deal prior to the 2019 season. He’s played for the club since ’11 but has only made the postseason once in ’14 and the organization has suffered through 11 straight losing seasons.
Trout, though, has been encouraged by some of the young talent both on the Major League roster and in the Minor Leagues, especially after being sellers at the Trade Deadline. Trout, who has a no-trade clause, remains optimistic as a result.
“The overall season, the record isn't where we want to be,” Trout said. “We had some positive storylines the last three months. I could go down the list of guys who had positive seasons and our pitching in the second half was unbelievable.”

item.content:encoded:
Corbin Carroll scalded an RBI double in Sunday’s season-ending loss to the Padres.

The Diamondbacks made an incredible run during the final week to push the Phillies to the brink, but they were unable to clear the final hurdle. Carroll was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the eighth inning once Arizona was officially eliminated from playoff contention following Philadelphia’s win over Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old franchise cornerstone battled a lingering back issue down the home stretch, but still managed to finish with 22 homers and 21 steals in 156 games. He’ll be an early-round selection in all fantasy leagues next spring.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

28 Sep 2026, 10:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Ed Szczepanski)
Rookie Lucas Spence ripped a two-run triple to highlight a four-run third inning, helping the Houston Astros celebrate the American League West title with a 9-0 victory over the Athletics on Sunday in West Sacramento, Calif.
Christian Walker homered to lead off the sixth inning and joined Yainer Diaz, Cam Smith and Jeremy Pena in collecting two hits and an RBI for the Astros (81-81), who won the division for the eighth time in the last 10 seasons.
Third-seeded Houston will host the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday in Game 1 of the best-of-three wild-card series. The Astros went 5-2 against the White Sox this season.
Houston actually captured the AL West title prior to the conclusion of its victory, as the Texas Rangers dropped a 6-4 decision to the Minnesota Twins on Sunday.
Yordan Alvarez went 1-for-4 with an RBI single to boost his batting average to .316, giving him his first batting title.
Lawrence Butler had two of the five hits for the Athletics (64-98), who lost for the ninth time in 12 games.
Phillies 7, Tampa Bay 3
Zack Wheeler pitched six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber drove in two runs as the Phillies clinched their fifth straight postseason berth by beating the Rays.
Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered for Philadelphia, which had lost its previous four games by the combined score of 23-3. The Phillies finally showed signs of life in Game 162, and now they'll head to Atlanta to face the Braves in the National League wild-card round that begins on Tuesday,
Johnny DeLuca homered twice for Tampa Bay. The Rays earned a bye into the American League Division Series and face the winner of the wild-card series between the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox.
Cubs 6, Red Sox 2
Alex Bregman went 4-for-4 with two home runs and four RBIs against his former team to help Chicago wrap up the regular season by defeating Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
The game was scheduled to be played in Boston, but was moved to Tropicana Field because of the nor'easter that hit much of New England throughout the weekend.
Both of Bregman's home runs came against Boston starter Tanner Houck, who made his first appearance on the mound since May 2025. Houck (0-1), who had Tommy John surgery last year, allowed three runs on four hits in three innings. The Red Sox were held to five hits and were 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position.
Twins 6, Rangers 4
Josh Bell hit a two-run home run and drove in three to lead host Minnesota to a season-ending win over Texas.
The loss eliminated the Rangers from the American League West title race and the playoffs. Rangers starter Mackenzie Gore allowed one hit and one run in 2 1/3 innings.
Twins starter Dean Kremer (5-5) gave up three hits and one run in seven innings. Kremer yielded a home run to Danny Jansen, but did not allow another Texas runner past first base.
Dodgers 5, Giants 1 (10 innings)
Andy Pages capped a four-run 10th inning with a three-run home run, and visiting Los Angeles beat San Francisco to earn its 100th win of the season.
The Dodgers took the lead in the 10th when Alex Call's two-out double off the left field fence drove in automatic runner Miguel Rojas. The Giants then elected to walk Max Muncy, before Pages foiled that strategy by driving a pitch by Duncan Davitt (0-1) into the left field bleachers for his 23rd home run of the season.
Alex Vesia (3-1), whose perfect ninth sent the game into the 10th, was credited with the win, which allows the Dodgers to take a three-game winning streak into their National League Division Series opener next Saturday against the winner of the wild-card series between the host Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies.
Marlins 5, Braves 3
Heriberto Hernandez and Griffin Conine slugged solo home runs, giving host Miami a win over Atlanta to end its season on a high note.
Marlins ace Sandy Alcantara tossed a scoreless ninth inning for his third career save. It was a fitting end of the year for Alcantara, who threw both the first and last pitch of the season for Miami. sStarter Janson Junk left with a no-decision. He allowed three hits and one run in 4 2/3 innings. Michael Petersen (4-4) earned the win with 1 1/3 hitless innings of relief.
Braves starter JR Ritchie (1-5) took the loss. He allowed seven hits and four runs in 5 2/3 innings. Mauricio Dubon hit his 12th homer to open the scoring and added an RBI single for Atlanta, which begins its home wild-card series against divisional rival Philadelphia on Tuesday.
Nationals 6, Mets 4
Andres Chaparro had three hits, including two solo home runs, and host Washington beat New York to end its season with a series win.
Will Dion (3-2) pitched two scoreless innings for the victory and Erik Tolman worked the ninth for his fifth save for Washington, which improved by 11 wins over 2025.
Francisco Lindor hit his 300th career homer and Ronny Mauricio smacked his third home run in two games for the Mets, who finished last in the National League East. Carson Benge ended his rookie season with three hits and an RBI.
Blue Jays 5, Reds 1
In potentially his final career start, Max Scherzer struck out seven over seven-plus innings and host Toronto topped Cincinnati.
The 42-year-old Scherzer (4-9) allowed one run and six hits to earn his 225th career win and boost his strikeout total to 3,557. The Blue Jays' 37-year-old designated hitter George Springer, who might have also played his last game, like Scherzer received a standing ovation when he was replaced.
Brandon Valenzuela hit a two-run home run for Toronto and Charles McAdoo added a solo shot in the rubber match of the three-game series. Brandon Williamson (5-5) allowed four runs and four hits in three innings for the Reds.
White Sox 4, Rockies 2
Randal Grichuk and Brenton Doyle smacked two-run home runs and Anthony Kay pitched five strong innings to boost host Chicago past Colorado.
The White Sox are set to visit the American League West champion Houston Astros on Tuesday in the opener of an AL wild-card series. Chicago clinched its first playoff berth on Thursday since 2021 but was eliminated from contention for an AL Central title with Saturday's loss to Colorado and a Cleveland victory at Kansas City.
Cole Carrigg homered for Colorado, which finished with more than 100 losses for the fourth successive season.
Royals 3, Guardians 2
Vinnie Pasquantino's second solo homer of the day broke an eighth-inning tie and sent host Kansas City to a win over Cleveland.
Jac Caglianone and Kyle Isbel each had two hits for the Royals, who ended a disappointing 2026 campaign by avoiding a sweep and winning for just the seventh time in the final 25 games.
Daniel Schneemann and Jo Adell each homered and had two hits apiece for the Guardians, who rested key regulars Steven Kwan, Jose Ramirez and Brayan Rocchio one day after securing their third consecutive American League Central title. Cleveland plays either the Chicago White Sox or Houston Astros in the American League Division Series.
Pirates 4, Tigers 2
Jared Jones pitched four innings of one-hit ball and Konnor Griffin led off the game with a solo home run and drove in two runs to lead Pittsburgh past host Detroit.
Griffin's homer was the sixth of his rookie season and helped the Pirates secure their first winning record since 2018 and only their second since last making the postseason in 2015. Jones was not eligible for the win after exiting the game before the fifth. Jones finished 5-6 with a 3.72 ERA in 21 starts after returning from elbow surgery in late May.
Rookie River Ryan (0-1) made his second start for the Tigers and sixth of his career. The right-hander allowed two runs on three hits over 1 1/3 innings. Detroit finished with a losing record after advancing to the American League Division Series each of the past two seasons.
Padres 9, Diamondbacks 4
Gavin Sheets homered and Freddy Fermin knocked in three runs as host San Diego tuned up for their National League wild-card series by stopping visiting Arizona.
San Diego, which opens its best-of-three series Tuesday night against the visiting Chicago Cubs, snapped a 4-4 tie with three runs in the bottom of the seventh. Fermin capped it with a two-run single.
Michael Soroka pitched 4 2/3 innings for Arizona, which was eliminated from postseason contention when Philadelphia beat Tampa Bay around the same time San Diego's Jake Cronenworth drew a bases-loaded walk to push home the go-ahead run in the seventh.
Brewers 6, Cardinals 4
Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his case for the National League Cy Young Award, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as host Milwaukee beat St. Louis to close with five consecutive wins and its franchise record for victories in a season (103).
Misiorowski (16-5) allowed two singles in 5 1/3 innings and lowered his major league-leading ERA to 1.80. The right-hander struck out five, giving him 252 strikeouts for the year.
Cardinals starter Andre Pallante (12-9) allowed six runs on 10 hits in five innings. He allowed six singles in the first inning for a 3-0 Brewers lead as well as Gary Sanchez's home run in the third.
Mariners 7, Angels 4
Logan Gilbert pitched four-plus hitless innings and struck out eight as host Seattle dealt Los Angeles its 100th loss of the season. It was also the last game for Dan Wilson as the Mariners' manager. The team announced after the game that Wilson will not return in that role in 2027 after a disappointing season and third-place finish in the American League West.
Jose Siri homered for the Angels, losers of 100 games for the first time. They had been the lone active MLB team to never suffer that many defeats.
Gilbert didn't allow a baserunner until walking Moises Ballesteros leading off the fifth. He struck out the side in the first inning to reach 200 strikeouts for the season, becoming the fourth pitcher in franchise history to do so in multiple seasons.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
5 men arrested near UK air base used by US in Iran war on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
LONDON (AP) — U.K. police said that five men arrested in the early hours of Sunday near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act that appeared to involve three trucks.
London’s Metropolitan Police, which takes the lead on potential terrorist activities, said police received a call at 12:45 a.m. related to the three suspicious vehicles that appeared to be traveling toward RAF Fairford, a U.K.-owned base that is operated by the U.S. under an agreement dating back to the Cold War.
The arrests come at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states to the U.K., with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil. In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states including Iran increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.
Fairford has been used by American bombers for strictly limited strikes against Iranian missile sites under an agreement with former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who voiced opposition to the war after it was launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28.
Authorities are investigating a link between the Fairford arrests and Iran as one possibility. Iran has previously indicated that a base used to attack its territory is a legitimate target.
Powerful nor’easter floods Northeast again, causing problems from New Jersey to New England
BOSTON (AP) — Residents of coastal communities in the Northeast slogged through floodwaters for a second day as a powerful nor’easter pummeled the shoreline Sunday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes.
Tidal surges swamped low-lying neighborhoods in New Jersey while wind gusts toppled trees on New York's Long Island, damaging homes and bringing down utility poles.
In the New Jersey beach town of Sea Bright, each high tide brought a new round of flooding. “It's not like a one-time occurrence,” said Caroline Virenius, whose garage filled with about a foot of water (30 centimeters). “It's getting wet again and again.”
The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City Housing Authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf all the way to New England.
Extreme amounts of rain — more than 4 inches (10 centimeters) since Friday in some spots in New Jersey — combined with a surging ocean led to flooding amounts not seen for close to a decade in places used to dealing with high water, residents said.
Mexico's Baja California braces for major Hurricane Polo as Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii
HILO, Hawaii (AP) — Hurricane Nolo edged further away from the Hawaiian Islands on Sunday as major Hurricane Polo bore down on Mexico's southern Baja California peninsula with a threat of storm surge, high winds and heavy rains.
Nolo was well southwest of Hawaii and moving away from the Big Island as the weekend drew to a close. A high-wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds increased to near 105 mph (165 kph).
Meanwhile, residents of Mexico's Baja California braced for the expected arrival Monday of Category 3 Polo, which had top sustained winds of 125 mph (205 kph) Sunday evening, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said. Heavy rainfall from Polo would begin impacting the peninsula overnight and could produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
Forecasters said Polo would hit the Mexican mainland after crossing Baja California and could bring heavy rain and flooding to parts of the U.S. Southwest later in the week. Polo was moving to the north at 12 mph (19 kph) about 270 miles (435 kilometers) west of Cabo San Lucas at the peninsula’s southern tip, the hurricane center said.
Forecasters said Nolo's outer bands could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides, with parts of the Big Island possibly getting up to 20 inches (50 centimeters) of rain. Heavy rain also was expected on the other islands.
Pope blasts assisted dying as 'false compassion' at French shrine known for miraculous cures
LOURDES, France (AP) — Pope Leo XIV on Sunday condemned the legalization of medically assisted death as immoral “false compassion,” reaffirming Catholic teaching on the sanctity of life during a visit to Lourdes, the French shrine associated with miraculous healings.
On the third day of his visit to France, Leo again waded into the end-of-life debate unfolding in his native U.S. and countries around the world. The issue roiled French politics for years before lawmakers recently approved legislation allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication.
Leo also met on Sunday with seven survivors of clergy sexual abuse, in what has now become a regular appointment for popes on foreign visits. The aim is to atone for the Catholic Church’s failure to protect its youngest and most vulnerable members from predator priests.
“It was extraordinary,” said survivor Jean-Marie Delbos, who joined four others at a press conference afterward to praise Leo for the encounter, saying he listened and was informed of their cases. “I never thought I would have a pope before me.”
Leo’s visit to the once staunchly Catholic and officially secular France has been marked by huge crowds — 800,000 at Leo’s Mass on Paris’ iconic Place de la Concorde — and his messaging against abortion and assisted dying.
Palestinian death toll in Gaza war passes 74,000, and other Mideast news
The Palestinian death toll from the nearly three-year Israel-Hamas war has surpassed 74,000, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran has not been formally notified of U.S. President Donald Trump's rejection of its proposed deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. And the World Health Organization says nearly 700 people have been killed in Yemen since fighting escalated last month.
Here is a look at the latest news from the Middle East on Sunday.
Araghchi said Tehran awaits a U.S. response through mediators after Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations.
Speaking from New York, Araghchi told NBC that Iran is “fully prepared for the war to be resumed."
Anthropic and OpenAI sound the alarm on AI safety — and seek to shape how it's controlled
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — As tech titans warned an AI-weary world that their own advanced systems could endanger humanity, the question emerged: What do they have to gain?
The answer may lie in the companies’ efforts to score political goals ahead of the U.S. midterm elections and the money top artificial intelligence labs and their investors stand to make in much-anticipated listings on a jittery stock market.
The CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI recently declared America’s cutting-edge models are so powerful, they’re dangerous, and need to be regulated and independently tested before being released. In a rare instance of unity, they have sketched alarming scenarios in essays, social media posts and speeches to the United Nations.
Along the way, they are shaping the conversation around how their technology should be controlled. With their rhetoric, the companies appear to be seeking public favor and to set the terms for their own safety protocols in the unregulated market, experts, analysts and former government evaluators told The Associated Press.
Those aims may not exactly align with what Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon sought when he quit via a post on X this month, calling for a pause on tech development to keep “superhuman” systems from eluding their makers' control. But the companies saw his post as an opportunity to highlight their own safety efforts and position themselves as cautious market leaders, just when they need fresh capital before going public on Wall Street.
Supreme Court vote shadows Maine Sen. Susan Collins in her first race after abortion rights decision
GORHAM, Maine (AP) — For years, Planned Parenthood’s endorsement of Susan Collins was enough to persuade Erin Evans to vote for Maine's longtime U.S. senator, believing that the moderate Republican would protect abortion access.
Evans is now “just furious with myself” for those votes. The 56-year-old from Portland described Collins’ critical vote to confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the U.S. Supreme Court, where President Donald Trump's nominee eventually helped overturn the constitutional right to abortion, as a betrayal.
“I was a really uninformed voter,” Evans said. “I thought any woman from Maine was probably in line with me.”
The Nov. 3 election will be the first time Collins is on the ballot since the Supreme Court’s 2022 ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade, resulting in abortion being banned in much of the United States. This time, Evans says she is backing Democrat Troy Jackson, a former state lawmaker and logger trying to deny Collins a sixth term.
Jackson and Democrats are hoping that voters like Evans will help flip a seat in a state the party has made a priority in the quest to retake the Senate.
From collapse to clinch, Phillies survive 'living hell' of last week and win final NL wild card
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Kyle Schwarber belly-flopped more than he actually slid headfirst into second base and popped up with his uniform smudged in dirt. He punched his right fist in the air and shouted something in exhilaration toward a fired-up Phillies dugout.
Schwarber delivered with a clutch two-run double, yes. He also showed the fire, the fight that vanished from the Phillies during a treacherous week that sent them from the brink of a wild-card clinch to the edge — and yes, the bottom was crumbling — of an all-time franchise collapse.
His slide had Phillies fans roaring from their feet — perhaps more than a few who wore brown paper bags over their heads a night earlier — and instantly all felt right on a soggy day inside Citizens Bank Park.
Zack Wheeler pitched a gem against Tampa Bay on Sunday and untangled a few thousand knots inside the stomachs of Phillies fans, and even from those inside a mostly solemn clubhouse. The Phillies survived their perilous five-day scare and are indeed headed to the playoffs for the fifth straight season after beating the Rays 7-3 to clinch the final NL wild-card berth.
“We didn't play the best baseball we could in September,” slugger Bryce Harper said. “Should we have clinched two weeks ago? Probably, right? But we didn't. We clinched today.”
Americans rally in singles to win the Presidents Cup for the 11th straight time
MEDINAH, Ill. (AP) — The deficit was larger than anything the Americans had ever experienced at home in the Presidents Cup. The celebration Sunday afternoon? That was all too familiar, even the part where President Donald Trump stuck around for the trophy presentation.
The U.S. players — from world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler to 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun — passed the gold cup down the line, which was only fitting.
Everyone had a hand in the latest comeback at Medinah, where the Americans delivered the most lopsided singles session in Presidents Cup history. They won nine of the 12 matches and halved the other for a 17-13 victory, their 11th in a row against the hard-luck Internationals.
U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker went from blaming himself for the three-point deficit to choking back emotions as his team set the tone early and rode momentum and a raucous Chicago gallery late that left them believing again they can succeed in team golf.
The real proof comes a year from now in Ireland for the Ryder Cup. For now, the Americans redeemed themselves in a competition they have lost only once since these matches began in 1994.
Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV VMAs history, dedicates top prize to Dolly Parton
NEW YORK (AP) — Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, as she is known to do.
The pop powerhouse received the inaugural Artist Director Honors on Sunday night, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.
Previously, she was tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. The new award is meant to recognize artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."
“I got to start making music videos and being a part of music videos 20 years ago,” Swift said in her speech, adding that she's been involved in making roughly 60 music videos, 18 of which she wrote and directed.
“You, the fans, make it so much fun,” she said.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 27, 2026, 9:08 PM ET
Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder Oneil Cruz (knee) did not play in his team's 4-2 win over the Detroit Tigers on Sunday due to a left knee contusion. However, Kevin Gorman of The Pittsburgh Tribune-Review reports that tests on Cruz's knee came back negative. The 27-year-old finishes 2026 hitting .280/.368/.486 with 20 home runs, 67 RBI, 65 runs scored, and 30 stolen bases across 419 plate appearances. Cruz missed over two months with a fractured hand, which may have cost him a chance at a truly elite fantasy season. The lefty slugger's .280 batting average is also likely a bit fluky, as he struck out in 33.2% of his plate appearances and batted .397 on balls in play. Still, Cruz carries elite power/speed upside for fantasy managers and profiles as one of the better outfield options for fantasy managers ahead of 2027.--Will Brady
Source: The Pittsburgh Tribune-Review - Kevin Gorman
More Recent News
Willson Contreras Back in Lineup for Sunday's Season Finale


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 12:39 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) is back in the starting lineup for the regular-season finale on Sunday against the visiting Chicago Cubs and left-hander Shota Imanaga, serving as the designated hitter and batting third for the BoSox, per MLB.com. It will be Contreras' first game played since being hit by a pitch on his hand last Thursday against the Texas Rangers, and he even expressed uncertainty recently about being ready for the Wild-Card series next week against the division-rival New York Yankees. The 34-year-old Venezuelan has had an excellent first year in Beantown, slashing .276/.387/.518 with a .905 OPS, a career-high 27 home runs, 81 RBI, 68 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 446 at-bats. However, he has played in only four games in September due to injury, and he could struggle at the plate as a result in the postseason if he is active. In 23 games in August, Contreras also struggled offensively, going 18-for-83 (.217) with three homers, 12 RBI, 11 walks, and 26 strikeouts across 98 plate appearances. He is hitless in eight career at-bats against Imanaga.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Juan Soto Back in Lineup for Season Finale


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:30 AM ET
New York Mets outfielder Juan Soto (hand) is starting in left field and will bat second for the 2026 season finale on Sunday against the division-rival Washington Nationals and left-hander DJ Herz, according to MLB.com. The Mets pulled Soto from Saturday's game early in D.C. after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch in the ninth inning, but thankfully, X-rays on his hand came back negative. The 27-year-old Dominican enters the final game of the season with only 395 at-bats in 2026 thanks to two separate trips to the injured list with calf injuries. When on the field for the Mets, though, the five-time All-Star continued to produce, slashing .278/.397/.522 with a .919 OPS, 27 home runs, 68 RBI, 63 runs scored, and nine stolen bases across 110 games and 477 plate appearances. Soto enters Sunday's contest with a .266 (25-for-94) average with five home runs and 14 RBI in 23 games played in the final month of the regular season. With better health next year, Soto is hoping that he can help get the Mets back into the postseason.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Kade Anderson Suffers Forearm Contusion on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:23 AM ET
Seattle Mariners rookie left-hander Kade Anderson (forearm) had X-rays come back negative after he was hit by a comebacker on his left forearm in his start on Saturday against the division-rival Los Angeles Angels, according to Daniel Kramer of MLB.com. Anderson and the Mariners avoided a significant scare in Anderson's final start of what has been a stellar debut season in the professional ranks. Before leaving after 3 1/3 innings of work at T-Mobile Park, Anderson did not allow a run on four hits while walking just one and striking out four to lower his season ERA to 3.79. The 22-year-old former third overall pick from LSU was as dominant as they come in the minors in 2026 before being called up to join Seattle's big-league starting rotation late in the year. In his seven starts for the M's, Anderson went 2-2 with a 3.79 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, and 32 strikeouts in 35 2/3 innings pitched. He dominated at Double-A Arkansas, posting a 1.06 ERA, 0.64 WHIP, and 135:13 K:BB in 18 starts over 93 1/3 frames. Anderson is one of the best young arms in all of baseball and should have a rotation spot locked up to begin the 2027 campaign.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Daniel Kramer
Jesus Luzardo Being Activated, Will be Available on Sunday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:17 AM ET
The Philadelphia Phillies will activate left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder) from the 15-day injured list on Sunday for the regular-season finale in a must-win game, interim manager Don Mattingly told Matt Gelb of The Athletic. Luzardo will be available out of the bullpen. The Phillies will have all hands on deck as they try to beat the Tampa Bay Rays to punch their ticket to the postseason as the final Wild-Card team in the National League. The 28-year-old Luzardo had been one of the best pitchers in baseball this year before landing on the IL with inflammation in his left shoulder back on Sept. 12. The native of Peru is returning to a 14-5 record, 2.87 ERA (2.78 FIP), a 1.08 WHIP, and a 221:52 K:BB in 178 2/3 innings pitched and 29 starts in his second season with the Phillies. Luzardo's strong 2026 campaign on the mound earned him his first career trip to the All-Star Game. If he is used in Sunday's game against Tampa, it could rule Luzardo out of starting a game in the Wild-Card series next week if the Phillies advance.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Matt Gelb
Griffin Jax Suffers Back Contusion on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:07 AM ET
The Tampa Bay Rays are saying that right-hander Griffin Jax (back) was removed from his appearance in Saturday's win over the Philadelphia Phillies due to a lower-back contusion, according to the Tampa Bay Times' Marc Topkin. Jax only made it three innings during his start at Citizens Bank Park, but he did not allow a run while giving up only two hits, walking none, and striking out one batter to lower his season ERA to 3.53. The 31-year-old veteran took a 104 mph liner off the bat of shortstop Trea Turner off his back in the third inning, and the Rays were not going to take any chances with Griffin. Manager Kevin Cash and Jax said after the game that he is not expected to miss any time, which means he should be available for the start of the American League Division Series against an undetermined opponent on Oct. 3. Jax finishes his first full season in Tampa with an 8-10 record, 3.53 ERA (3.76 FIP) and 1.17 WHIP with a career-high 116 strikeouts and 35 walks in 112 1/3 innings across 34 outings (23 starts). He began the 2026 season as Tampa's primary ninth-inning arm before making a successful transition to the rotation.--Keith Hernandez

Chandler Simpson Unlikely to Play Until ALDS

Simpson did not play in the team's win over the Philadelphia Phillies on Saturday and likely will not play in the regular-season finale on Sunday "to take precautions." He is fully confident that he will be good to go for the American League Division Series opener on Oct. 3. Simpson will end his 2026 season with a strong .306/.333/.356 slash line with a .689 OPS, zero home runs, 38 RBI, a league-leading 46 stolen bases, and 66 runs scored in 151 games played across 612 plate appearances in only his second season in the majors. Sep 26, 2026, 6:58 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (foot) is not in the team's starting lineup for Saturday's game in Philadelphia against the Phillies, per MLB.com. Victor Mesa Jr. is starting in left field for the Rays and is batting fifth against Phillies right-hander Aaron Nola. The Rays are being cautious with the speedster, giving him a day off in Game 2 of the series at Citizens Bank Park after Simpson fouled a ball off his right foot during the win on Friday night. The Rays already have a first-round bye locked up in the American League, so Simpson will have plenty of time to heal before the start of the AL Division Series. If the 25-year-old does not play in the regular-season finale on Sunday, he will finish his second big-league season in 2026 with a very nice .306/.333/.356 slash line, .689 OPS, zero home runs, 38 RBI, and 66 runs scored across 151 games and 612 plate appearances. Simpson has no power to speak of, but he leads the league with 46 stolen bases after swiping 44 bags as a rookie in 2025. His speed in the outfield and on the basepaths is a game-changer for the first-place Rays.--Keith Hernandez

Juan Soto Hit by Pitch on his Hand, X-Rays Come Back Negative


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 5:28 PM ET
New York Mets superstar outfielder Juan Soto (hand) left Saturday's game against the division-rival Washington Nationals early after being hit on the right hand by a 91.7 mph sinker, according to Anthony DiComo of MLB.com. Soto was in some clear discomfort, but X-rays on his hand came back negative. Before leaving the game, Soto went 2-for-4 at the plate with a strikeout. He was replaced in left field by Nick Morabito. It sounds like Soto avoided a serious injury, but with just one more game in the 2026 regular season, the Mets might hold the left-handed slugger out to close out another disappointing season for the Mets. The 27-year-old five-time All-Star and six-time Silver Slugger winner missed extended time this year with two separate calf injuries, but he still came into Saturday's contest with a solid .276/.395/.522 slash line, .917 OPS, 27 home runs, 68 RBI, 63 runs scored, and nine stolen bases across his 391 at-bats. With better health in 2027, Soto could quickly get back to elite five-category production for his fantasy managers.--Keith Hernandez

Sep 26, 2026, 2:09 PM ET
Miami Marlins outfielder Kyle Stowers (abdomen) is out of the lineup on Saturday due to an abdominal injury. The 28-year-old has been battling through injuries all season long, and this latest ailment comes on the heels of his absence from Friday's lineup. Sep 26, 2026, 1:53 PM ET

He has made just two rehab appearances, striking out five batters over 3.2 scoreless innings across various minor league levels. He also tossed a two-inning simulated game last week, giving the Tigers enough confidence to put him on the mound for the final day of the regular season. Should he pitch effectively without any setbacks, this would be a good "peace-of-mind" way to finish the year and head into a normal offseason. Sep 26, 2026, 1:37 PM ET

A pitch hit the 28-year-old in the first inning of a pivotal game against Minnesota, and the testing later confirmed the injury. He will miss time while he heals, ending his 2026 season on a sour note. Still, despite battling multiple injuries all season, he will finish with a .299 batting average and 12 home runs over 104 games. While nothing has been confirmed, it would appear that he will be ready for Spring Training next season. Elmer Rodriguez to Pitch on Sunday for Yankees


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 12:47 PM ET
New York Yankees right-handed pitching prospect Elmer Rodriguez will pitch on Sunday against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles in the final game of the 2026 regular season, weather permitting, according to Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. He had five of his six saves on the year in Toronto, but also an ERA near 4.00. Although Hoffman was used as more of a late-inning setup man after being acquired in a trade by Minnesota, he fared better in his 20 relief outings with the Twins, with a 2.50 ERA, 1.17 WHIP, and 27:12 K:BB in 18 innings pitched. Kaelen Culpepper Returns From Injured List on Saturday

Outfielder Jesus Sanchez was designated for assignment to open up a spot on the roster. In the Snakes' 11-4 victory on Friday night, Moreno went 2-for-3 at the plate with an RBI, two runs scored, and a walk before being replaced behind the dish by James McCann. The D-backs can ill-afford to lose their starting catcher with just two games remaining in the regular season, as the Venezuelan backstop is hitting over .300 on the year with 16 home runs. Sep 25, 2026, 10:00 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Andrew Vaughn (illness) was placed on the 10-day Injured List on Friday, retroactive to Tuesday. In a corresponding move, outfielder Brandon Lockridge has been recalled to give the Brewers a fresh body for the final few games of the regular season.--Andy Webb

Sep 25, 2026, 9:53 PM ET
Arizona Diamondbacks starting pitcher Corbin Burnes (shoulder) was placed on the 15-day Injured List on Friday. Burnes was expected to make his final start of the season on Sunday, but instead, he'll go to the shelf due to right shoulder inflammation. Burnes only made three starts this season as he missed most of the year while recovering from Tommy John surgery. He was lit up for a 7.84 ERA and 1.55 WHIP across his 10.1 innings of work this season. The D-Backs still have a chance to make the postseason, so there's a chance that Burnes can contribute in October. Source: Arizona Diamondbacks
Chandler Simpson Exits with Foot Injury


Andy Webb




Sep 25, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (foot) was forced to make an early exit during Friday's game against the Philadelphia Phillies, Marc Topkin reports. Simpson sustained an injury after fouling a ball off his foot in the sixth inning. He attempted to stay in the game, but he was pulled in the seventh inning. He was hitless during his three plate appearances during the victory over the Phillies. The expectation is that he'll undergo imaging to determine the severity of the injury. item.title: [mlb.com] Phillies put tumultuous week behind them to punch playoff ticket
item.dc:creator: Todd Zolecki
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Phillies celebrated. They popped champagne and beer bottles, smoked cigars and blared music in the home clubhouse on Sunday evening at Citizens Bank Park. It felt cathartic. It represented a fresh start. Last week, the Phillies had a four-game lead over Arizona for the final NL Wild Card spot with five games to play, and no team since postseason play began in 1903 had blown a lead like that. But the Phillies stumbled. They lost four in a row, while Arizona won four in a row.
item.content:encoded:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Phillies celebrated.
They popped champagne and beer bottles, smoked cigars and blared music in the home clubhouse on Sunday evening at Citizens Bank Park. It felt cathartic. It represented a fresh start. Last week, the Phillies had a four-game lead over Arizona for the final NL Wild Card spot with five games to play, and no team since postseason play began in 1903 had blown a lead like that.
But the Phillies stumbled. They lost four in a row, while Arizona won four in a row. Suddenly, the Phils needed to beat the Rays on the final day of the 162-game season to punch their ticket to the postseason and avoid being immortalized alongside the 1964 Phillies, who infamously blew a 6 1/2-game lead with 12 to play to lose the NL pennant to St. Louis.
So, they partied. It’s what baseball teams do when they clinch.
“It’s so hard to get here,” Trea Turner said. “We had such an up and down here as a whole team. We were talking about it in the cage earlier today. I think this is the first time I've ever had to play like 162. First time ever, 162 has counted for, you know, a big deal. So I think it's kind of a rare situation, and I'm glad we got the job done.”
It has been a long, trying season in Philadelphia. So regardless of how anybody felt about the past several weeks -- and nobody could argue they played poorly at times -- the Phillies always planned to celebrate this moment.
Gloria Gaynor’s “I Will Survive” was the first song to play in the clubhouse. It was fitting.
“Everything resets,” Bryce Harper said. “You get into October and everything resets obviously.
“We’re the type of team that, you know, we don’t care … like I said, people’s opinions of us or what they think or what anybody thinks about our team. I mean, we're going to go in and do our job and we need to do our job. Obviously, we didn't play the best baseball we could in September. Should we have clinched two weeks ago? Probably. Right? But we didn’t. You know, we clinched today, and that's how the story's written right now.”
The Phillies started the season at 9-19, costing manager Rob Thomson his job on April 28. Don Mattingly took his place.
The Phillies not only rebounded, but they had one of the best records in baseball for months. They looked like a postseason threat, too, because they had Jesús Luzardo, Cristopher Sánchez and Zack Wheeler pitching well atop the rotation and because the offense finally seemed to click following Luis Arraez’s arrival from the Giants on Aug. 3.
But then they stumbled. The offense went from one of the best in baseball in August to one of the worst in September. They scored three runs during the four-game losing streak, which included a 21-inning scoreless streak.
Fans booed.
He allowed one run in six innings as the Phillies took a 7-1 lead.
“We know who we are,” Wheeler said. “We just gotta play like it. At the beginning and at the end, we didn't play like it so much. So we gotta turn it up. We gotta be ready for Atlanta.”
Bryson Stott, starting in the cleanup spot for just the seventh time in his career, hit a two-out double in the first inning to score a run to give the Phillies a 1-0 lead. J.T. Realmuto snapped an 0-for-34 slump with a double to score a run in the second to make it 2-0. Kyle Schwarber’s two-out double scored two runs to make it 4-0.
Harper’s homer in the fifth was the team’s first since Tuesday and Harper’s first since Sept. 12.
Fans cheered.
“Today, that was one of our better crowds, I thought,” Mattingly said. “You don't hear a lot of, ‘Let's go, Phillies!’" at our games. It's just waiting for things. Right? It'd be great if it would be like an uplifting-type scenario. In the Milwaukee series, somebody makes an out in the fourth with a guy on base, and it's like a boo. And I know it's the fans' right to do it, but it's like, you can either lift up or you can hold down, and if you lift the team up, you’ve got a game.”
Alex McFarlane allowed two runs in the seventh, then Luzardo pitched the eighth. He might have been the Phillies’ best pitcher this season, but he hadn’t pitched since Sept. 7 because of inflammation in his left shoulder.
Sunday was the first time he had faced hitters since then.
He retired the side on four pitches. He looked great. He said he’s available to start this week, if asked. If not, he’ll be available in the bullpen. The same is true for Andrew Painter, who is also in play to start this week.
Wheeler? He could pitch in Atlanta, too.
“I feel like I'm prepared to give the team whatever they ask, whatever they need,” Luzardo said.
The Phillies will need to get creative with their pitching to beat Atlanta. They will need their hitters to show up and beat Chris Sale on Tuesday.
It’s not impossible.
“The past is the past,” Luzardo said. “You play 162 games for a reason. I think this team has what it takes, and we obviously showed it throughout a full season. I don't think the last four days are indicative of what we can do. I think today was and I think that we look forward to Tuesday starting with a clean slate.”

item.title: [이투데이] MLB 포스트시즌 30일 개막⋯김하성ㆍ송성문ㆍ김혜성 출전할까

미국프로야구 메이저리그(MLB) 2026시즌 정규리그가 28일(한국시간) 끝났다. 포스트시즌은 30일 와일드카드시리즈로 시작한다. 김하성이 속한 애틀랜타 브레이브스와 송성문이 속한 샌디에이고 파드리스는 와일드카드시리즈부터 나서고, 김혜성이 속한 LA 다저스는 디비전시리즈에 직행했다.
와일드카드시리즈는 3전 2승제로 열린다. 아메리칸리그(AL)에서는 휴스턴 애스트로스와 시카고 화이트삭스, 뉴욕 양키스와 보스턴 레드삭스가 맞붙는다. 두 대진의 승자는 각각 클리블랜드 가디언스, 탬파베이 레이스와 디비전시리즈를 치른다.
내셔널리그(NL)에서는 애틀랜타와 필라델피아 필리스, 샌디에이고와 시카고 컵스가 격돌한다. 애틀랜타–필라델피아 승자는 다저스를, 샌디에이고–컵스 승자는 밀워키 브루어스를 만난다. 디비전시리즈는 5전 3승제로 진행된다.
포스트시즌 진출팀에 속한 한국 선수는 김하성ㆍ송성문ㆍ김혜성 등 3명이다. 세 선수가 경기에 나설 자격을 얻을지는 각 팀의 시리즈별 로스터가 발표된 뒤 확인할 수 있다.
김하성은 이날 마이애미 말린스와의 정규리그 최종전에 7번 타자 유격수로 나서 2타수 무안타 2볼넷 1득점을 기록했다. 올 시즌 타율은 0.116으로, 홈런 없이 9타점을 올렸다.
송성문도 애리조나 다이아몬드백스와의 최종전에 8번 타자 유격수로 출전해 3타수 무안타 1볼넷 1득점을 기록했다. 빅리그 데뷔 시즌 성적은 타율 0.191, 1홈런, 17타점, 13도루다.
김혜성은 5월 말 마이너리그로 내려간 뒤 빅리그에 복귀하지 못했다. 올 시즌 타율 0.259, 1홈런, 11타점, 5도루로 정규리그를 마쳤다. 다저스가 디비전시리즈에 직행한 가운데 김혜성이 포스트시즌 로스터에 이름을 올릴지 주목된다.
한편 이정후가 속한 샌프란시스코 자이언츠는 포스트시즌에 진출하지 못했다. 이정후는 최근 사타구니 타박상으로 부상자 명단에 올라 정규리그를 마쳤다.

AI 핵심 요약
beta
- MLB가 28일 포스트시즌 대진을 확정했다.
- AL은 탬파베이·클리블랜드가 DS 직행했다.
- NL은 밀워키·다저스가 DS에 선착했다.
!AI가 자동 생성한 요약으로 정확하지 않을 수 있어요.
[서울=뉴스핌] 박상욱 기자 = 미국프로야구 메이저리그(MLB)가 팀당 162경기의 대장정을 마무리하고 본격적인 가을야구 체제에 돌입했다.
휴스턴 애스트로스가 정규리그 마지막 날 아메리칸리그(AL) 서부지구 1위를 확정하면서 2026시즌 포스트시즌 진출을 확정한 양대 리그 12개 팀의 최종 대진표가 완성됐다.
아메리칸리그에서는 동부지구 1위 탬파베이 레이스가 AL 1번 시드, 중부지구 챔피언 클리블랜드 가디언스가 2번 시드를 받아 디비전시리즈(DS·5전 3승제)에 직행했다. 지구 우승 팀 중 승률이 낮은 휴스턴(3번 시드)은 와일드카드 3위 시카고 화이트삭스(6번 시드)와 맞붙는다. 또 다른 와일드카드 매치업으로는 뉴욕 양키스(4번 시드)와 보스턴 레드삭스(5번 시드)가 격돌한다. 와일드카드시리즈(WC·3전 2승제) 승자들은 각각 클리블랜드와 탬파베이를 상대로 DS 치열한 승부를 벌인다.
내셔널리그(NL)에서는 중부지구 1위 밀워키 브루어스가 전체 승률 1위로 1번 시드, 서부지구 1위 로스앤젤레스 다저스가 2번 시드를 거머쥐며 디비전시리즈에 직행했다. 동부지구 1위 애틀랜타 브레이브스(3번 시드)는 와일드카드 3위 필라델피아 필리스(6번 시드)와, 샌디에이고 파드리스(4번 시드)는 시카고 컵스(5번 시드)와 와일드카드시리즈에서 맞대결한다. 이 승자들은 각각 다저스와 밀워키와 만난다.
한국인 메이저리거들이 포스트시즌 로스터에 포함되어 가을야구 무대를 밟을지에도 관심이 쏠린다. 애틀랜타의 김하성은 이날 마이애미 말린스와의 최종전에 7번 타자 유격수로 출전해 2타수 2볼넷 1삼진 1득점을 기록해 타율 0.116으로 시즌을 마감했다. 샌디에이고의 송성문은 데뷔 시즌 타율 0.191, 1홈런, 17타점, 13도루를 기록했다. 다저스의 김혜성은 빅리그 2년 차를 타율 0.259, 1홈런, 11타점, 5도루로 마무리했다.
올해 MLB 포스트시즌은 오는 30일부터 10월 2일까지 열리는 와일드카드시리즈로 막을 올린다. 와일드카드시리즈는 상위 시드 팀의 홈구장에서 3전 2선승제로 치러진다. 이후 10월 4일부터 11일까지 디비전시리즈가 열리며, 7전 4선승제의 리그 챔피언십시리즈(LCS)는 10월 12일부터 21일까지 진행된다. 대망의 월드시리즈(7전 4선승제)는 10월 24일 막을 올리며 정규시즌 승률이 더 높은 팀이 홈 어드밴티지를 쥔다.

item.title: [MLB.com] Recuperado del rostro, Bregman pega 2 jonrones en su 2do juego de regreso
item.dc:creator: Jordan Bastian
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG -- Incluso sin nada en juego en cuanto a la postemporada el domingo, Alex Bregman le dijo al manager de los Cachorros, Craig Counsell, que quería estar en la alineación titular. El antesalista consideraba importante sumar más turnos al bate de cara a los playoffs. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG -- Incluso sin nada en juego en cuanto a la postemporada el domingo, Alex Bregman le dijo al manager de los Cachorros, Craig Counsell, que quería estar en la alineación titular. El antesalista consideraba importante sumar más turnos al bate de cara a los playoffs.
Y si quedaba alguna duda sobre cómo Bregman estaba viendo la pelota apenas una semana después del inusual foul que le provocó múltiples fracturas en la mejilla izquierda, ofreció una respuesta contundente contra los Medias Rojas. Apenas en su segundo juego de regreso a la alineación, Bregman disparó dos contundentes jonrones en sus primeros dos turnos al bate en el Tropicana Field.
Después de disputar dos juegos el viernes en el Fenway Park, donde los fuertes vientos relacionados con la tormenta del nordeste que azotaba la región afectaron considerablemente a la ofensiva de Chicago, el traslado a una sede neutral le dio a la alineación la oportunidad de empezar de cero. Eso era especialmente importante para Bregman, quien se fue de 4-0 en su primer partido de regreso, en el primer encuentro de la doble cartelera del viernes.
“Sentí como si no hubiera jugado en varios días, pero mi rostro estaba bien”, dijo Bregman el viernes. “Vi bien la pelota. Así que espero poder aprovechar esos turnos y volver a sentirme como me sentía antes”.
Si lo ocurrido el domingo sirve como indicio, el swing de Bregman luce en buena forma de cara a la próxima Serie del Comodín de la Liga Nacional contra los Padres.
La única interrogante en estos momentos es si Counsell volverá a colocar a Bregman en la tercera base durante la postemporada o si, por ahora, lo mantendrá como bateador designado. Bregman ha sido el BD en sus primeros dos juegos de regreso, y Counsell dio indicios de que podría mantenerlo en ese rol como una manera de reducir el riesgo de un contratiempo.
Bregman tomó rodados durante una práctica en el Tropicana Field en el día libre del sábado, pero Counsell está evaluando la situación día a día a la hora de considerar su regreso a la defensa.
“Tenemos que tomar una decisión al respecto, sin duda”, dijo Counsell. “Simplemente veremos cómo se siente cada día. Creo que mejora día tras día, pero tiene múltiples fracturas faciales y ha pasado [una semana]. Así que veremos cómo se siente. Una de las cosas en las que estoy pensando es el riesgo de exponerlo más.
“Creo que sus turnos al bate son lo más importante que podemos obtener. Entonces, ¿vale la pena esa exposición? ¿Nos hace realmente mucho mejores a costa de poner en riesgo esos turnos? Eso es lo que tenemos que considerar. Y, por supuesto, también la salud y el bienestar del jugador”.
Bregman conectó cuadrangulares en el primer y tercer innings, primero ante un sinker en el primer pitcheo y luego frente a un sweeper con cuenta de 0-1, enviando ambos lanzamientos a las gradas del jardín izquierdo. Fueron los vuelacercas 27 y 28 del año para Bregman, quien ha sido uno de los mejores bateadores del béisbol en la segunda mitad de la temporada. Antes del último juego de la campaña regular, sólo Pete Crow-Armstrong (4.7), los dominicanos Fernando Tatis Jr. (3.7) y Elly De La Cruz (3.6) tenían un WAR más alto, según FanGraphs, que Bregman (3.3) desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Bregman agregó un sencillo en el quinto episodio, negoció un boleto en el séptimo y sumó un doble productor en el noveno. Cuando llegó a base después de esos turnos, Bregman cambió un casco, que tenía una extensión sobre la oreja izquierda, por otro con una protección más larga a cada lado para brindarle mayor seguridad.
Bregman se encontraba en el círculo de espera el 20 de septiembre en Cincinnati cuando recibió en el rostro una pelota de foul bateada por Michael Busch. Antes de ese juego, el antesalista de los Cachorros había bateado .298 con 19 jonrones, 18 dobles, 53 carreras impulsadas y OPS de 1.000 en sus 60 encuentros anteriores. Durante ese período, su OPS de la temporada subió de .670 a .801.
“Estoy entusiasmado por la postemporada. Tengo muchas ganas de que llegue”, dijo Bregman el viernes. “Siento que hoy se trataba de tomar algunos turnos al bate y volver a entrar en ritmo. Quería asegurarme de no estar pensando en nada relacionado con mi rostro y de que lo único que pasara por mi mente fuera lo mismo en lo que normalmente pienso cuando juego béisbol. Y así fue. No pensé en eso ni una sola vez”.

item.dc:creator: Bobby Blanco
item.description: WASHINGTON -- Francisco Lindor had been waiting to reach the 300-home run milestone for a while now. item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON -- Francisco Lindor had been waiting to reach the 300-home run milestone for a while now. The Mets’ star shortstop was riding a 13-game homerless streak into Game 162 against the Nationals. He had last hit a long ball on Sept. 12, when he actually launched two homers out of Yankee Stadium.
But Lindor didn’t have to wait too much longer once the season’s last game finally got underway after a one-hour rain delay at Nationals Park on Sunday.
Lindor launched career home run No. 300 in the top of the second inning during the Mets' 6-4 loss to the Nationals. His 21st of the season came off Nationals left-hander DJ Herz, traveling a Statcast-projected 409 feet to left field at 110.8 mph off the bat.
Per the Elias Sports Bureau, Lindor is the fifth player to have played at least 50 percent of his games at shortstop at the time of his 300th home run, joining Ernie Banks, Cal Ripken Jr., Alex Rodriguez and Miguel Tejada.
Lindor also became the 11th switch-hitter with at least 300 homers in his career, and the second of those with 200 stolen bases as well, joining Carlos Beltrán.
Lindor’s homer was the second of back-to-back jacks hit by the Mets in the second inning after Ronny Mauricio homered in his third straight at-bat dating back to the two he hit in Saturday’s 7-1 win.
