item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE -- Cada día de apertura era un evento cuando Jacob Misiorowski se subía al montículo durante la temporada regular de 103 victorias de los Cerveceros, una cifra récord para la franquicia. Hasta el último encuentro.
El as de 24 años de Milwaukee recibió una ovación mientras trotaba hacia el dugout para calentar, y otra cuando salió del montículo tras su último calentamiento de cara a la postemporada en la victoria de los Cerveceros por 6-4 el domingo en el American Family Field, tras ponchar al estelar guardabosque de los Cardenales, Jordan Walker, para cerrar con broche de oro una de las campañas más dominantes en la historia.
Con 5.1 entradas en blanco adicionales de dos hits y dos boletos, con cinco ponches y una recta que alcanzó hasta las 102.7 mph, el as de 6 pies 7 pulgadas de los Cerveceros terminó como el líder de las Grandes Ligas en efectividad (1.80), ponches (252), WHIP (0.80) y promedio de sus oponentes (.157) en 174.2 electrizantes entradas.
Se unió a Corbin Burnes (2021) como los únicos lanzadores en la historia de la franquicia de Milwaukee en ganar el título de efectividad de MLB, y se unió a Justin Verlander (2019) y al dominicano Pedro Martínez (2000) como los únicos serpentineros en la historia con más de 250 ponches y WHIP de al menos 0.80. Y según Elias Sports Bureau, Misiorowski se unió a Sandy Koufax (1965), J.R. Richard (1976) y Mike Scott (1986) como los únicos pitchers desde 1950 en encabezar las Mayores en efectividad, ponches y promedio de sus oponentes.
Podrías seguir señalando estadísticas. Los Cerveceros terminaron con el mejor récord en todo el béisbol con 103-59, y no hubo duda alguna sobre quién encabezó el cuerpo de pitcheo.
Aquí hay algunas otras medidas récord de lanzadores que registraron al menos 170 entradas en una temporada:
Tasa de ponches
- 39.9% Gerrit Cole (2019)
- 37.9% Misiorowski (2026)
- 37.5% Pedro Martínez (1999)
- 37.4% Randy Johnson (2001)
- 36.8% Spencer Strider (2023)
WHIP
- 0.74 Pedro Martínez (2000)
- 0.78 Walter Johnson (1913)
- 0.80 Misiorowski (2026)
- 0.80 Justin Verlander (2019)
- 0.81 Addie Joss (1908)
Promedio de sus oponentes
- .157 Misiorowski (2026)
- .167 Pedro Martínez (2000)
- .168 Luis Tiant (1968)
- .171 Nolan Ryan (1972)
- .172 Nolan Ryan (1991)
- .172 Justin Verlander (2019)
Para la efectividad, usaremos 1969 como punto de partida, debido a que fue el año en que MLB bajó el montículo a su altura actual en respuesta al Año del Lanzador en 1968. Aquí es donde encaja Misiorowski entre las mejores efectividades desde entonces entre serpentineros que registraron al menos 170 episodios:
- 1.53 Dwight Gooden (1985)
- 1.56 Greg Maddux (1994)
- 1.63 Greg Maddux (1995)
- 1.66 Zack Greinke (2015)
- 1.70 Jacob deGrom (2018)
- 1.74 Pedro Martínez (2000)
- 1.74 Ron Guidry (1978)
- 1.75 Justin Verlander (2022)
- 1.76 Tom Seaver (1971)
- 1.77 Jake Arrieta (2015)
- 1.80 Misiorowski (2026)
- 1.82 Vida Blue (1971)
- 1.83 Clayton Kershaw (2014)
- 1.87 Roger Clemens (2005)

item.title: [LancasterOnline] Alex Bregman's huge day at the plate in relocated season finale powers Cubs to 6-2 win over Red Sox

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Alex Bregman went 4 for 4 with two home runs and four RBIs in his second game back from a frightening injury, and the Chicago Cubs beat the Boston Red Sox 6-2 on Sunday in a regular-season finale that was relocated to Tropicana Field.
Chicago is the No. 5 seed in the National League playoffs and will play a best-of-three Wild Card Series at fourth-seeded San Diego beginning Tuesday night.
Boston is the No. 5 seed in the American League playoffs and will travel to New York to open its Wild Card Series the same night against the rival Yankees.
Major League Baseball moved the Cubs-Red Sox season finale to Florida because of a weekend nor’easter that was expected to batter the Boston area into Monday. Ahead of the storm, the Red Sox swept a doubleheader from the Cubs on Friday at Fenway Park.
Bregman went 0 for 4 with a strikeout at designated hitter in the opener — five days after sustaining facial fractures when he was struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle.
The three-time All-Star third baseman, who played for Boston last year, was the DH again Sunday and fared much better at the plate in his final postseason tuneup. In addition to finishing a triple shy of the cycle, he drew a walk and scored three times.
With the NL MVP award virtually locked up, Pete Crow-Armstrong singled to open the game before Cubs manager Craig Counsell immediately removed him for pinch-runner Tyrone Taylor. Bregman launched the next pitch from Tanner Houck (0-1) into the left-field seats.
Adley Rutschman hit a solo homer off Chicago starter Shota Imanaga, who was lifted after one inning with postseason seeding already decided.
Braxton Garrett (1-1) pitched five strong innings in relief for his first win since May 29, 2024. Colin Rea earned his second save.
Played at the home of the Tampa Bay Rays, the game drew 20,411 fans who had less than 48 hours’ notice to purchase tickets.
Chicago finished 89-73, three games shy of its 92-70 mark in 2025.
Boston, which was 89-73 in 2025, ended the season 87-75. The Red Sox fired manager Alex Cora following a 10-17 start and replaced him with Chad Tracy.
Under Tracy, Boston became the first team to qualify for the postseason after dropping as many as 44 of its initial 75 games.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Jacob Misiorowski makes Cy Young case as Brewers down Cardinals
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his Cy Young case, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as the Milwaukee Brewers built momentum for the postseason with a 6-4 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday. Milwaukee (103-59), which has clinched a first-round Wild Card bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, closed with five consecutive wins to extend its franchise record for victories in a season. Milwaukee, the first team to win four consecutive NL Cent
item.content:encoded:
Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his Cy Young case, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as the Milwaukee Brewers built momentum for the postseason with a 6-4 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday.
Milwaukee (103-59), which has clinched a first-round Wild Card bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, closed with five consecutive wins to extend its franchise record for victories in a season.
Milwaukee, the first team to win four consecutive NL Central titles, finished 35-17 against division rivals and went 18-6 in September.
St. Louis (77-85) scored four runs in the eighth off Chad Patrick to pull within 6-4, capped by Leo Bernal’s three-run homer. Shane Drohan got the final five outs for his second save.
Misiorowski (16-5) allowed two singles in 5 1/3 innings, departing after striking out Jordan Walker in the sixth to end a 68-pitch outing, lowering his major league-leading ERA to 1.80. Misiorowski struck out five and walked two, giving him 252 strikeouts for the year.
Misiorowski is the second Brewers pitcher to lead the league in ERA, joining Corbin Burnes (2021).
Milwaukee bunched six singles off Andre Pallante in the first inning for a 3-0 lead. Garrett Mitchell, Jake Bauers and Jackson Chourio opened with consecutive singles for the first run. Brice Turang reached on a run-scoring infield single, giving him 100 RBIs for the season. Christian Yelich singled in another run.
Gary Sanchez put the Brewers up 5-0 with one out in the third with his 12th home run following a leadoff single by Chourio.
Chourio’s RBI single in the fourth made it 6-0.
St. Louis rallied in the eighth when Cesar Prieto triple to open and Pedro Pages walked. Prieto scored on Jordan Walker’s fielder’s choice grounder. Ivan Herrera walked and Bernal followed with his fifth homer.
Pallante (12-9) allowed six runs on 10 hits in five innings, striking out four and walking one.
St. Louis, which has not made the postseason since 2022 and has not won a playoff series since the NLDS in 2019, was 50-45 at the All-Star break, but went 27-40 the rest of the way.
–Field Level Media

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Mets’ Francisco Lindor Makes Rare Baseball History
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The New York Mets' season is ending on Sunday. They have been out of the playoff picture for a long while, and so the final day of the 2026 MLB regular season is all she wrote for the Mets. There won't be a lot they want to remember about what happened this year, but one player continued to be a leader as best he could: Francisco Lindor. That included helping the Mets put up some runs on Sunday. If they were going to have the season end, they might as well hit the ball around the yard a bit more
item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets' season is ending on Sunday.
They have been out of the playoff picture for a long while, and so the final day of the 2026 MLB regular season is all she wrote for the Mets.
There won't be a lot they want to remember about what happened this year, but one player continued to be a leader as best he could: Francisco Lindor.
That included helping the Mets put up some runs on Sunday. If they were going to have the season end, they might as well hit the ball around the yard a bit more.
Lindor didn't just hit it around, either — he left the yard altogether, and it was a historic moment.
Francisco Lindor Makes Rare History
Lindor's home run on Sunday was a milestone for those who appreciate round numbers: He now has 300 home runs.
It makes Lindor the fourth infielder in MLB history with at least 300 home runs and 200 stolen bases.
Lindor has 219 steals to go with his now-300 homers.
He joins a list that also includes Alex Rodriguez, Jeff Bagwell and George Brett.
A-Rod has the most of both stats on this particular list — he hit 696 home runs and stolen 329 bases.
Bagwell ended his MLB career with 449 homers and 202 steals.
Brett just cleared the steals threshold, too, swiping 201 bags while blasting 317 homers.
Lindor joins two Hall of Famers, as well as one of the most talented players of all time in Rodriguez — whose absence from the Hall of Fame has nothing to do with his ability.
Francisco Lindor Future
The big question entering the offseason with Lindor is whether he'll be with the Mets for the long run.
A season ago, the Mets had a brutal collapse to miss the playoffs in the final week of the season.
This year, the Mets never were really even in the picture.
Yes, that also correlates with the signing of Juan Soto to a mega contract, but Lindor has obviously been a part of it, too.
What are the Mets supposed to do? They know that Lindor is still a special player — just as Soto is. But there also feels like there needs to be a vibes change heading into the 2027 season.
There's the added complication this offseason that there could be a lockout that delays the winter action as well as potentially the start of the 2027 season.
So there will be plenty of talking points beyond Lindor. Still, it's worth considering what his future looks like. He can still get the job done, but the Mets are going to want to be a lot better next season, however they can find a way to do that.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Mets' Francisco Lindor Makes Rare Baseball History appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Bleed Cubbie Blue] Cubs 6, Red Sox 2: Alex Bregman is more than ready for the postseason
item.dc:creator: Al Yellon
item.description: Last Sunday, Alex Bregman was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch in Cincinnati. He suffered facial fractures and missed three games. Bregman came back Friday as the DH and Sunday, just a bit over exactly one week since that accident, he hit two home runs and also singled, doubled and walked. His 4-for-4 afternoon led the Cubs to a 4-2 Game 162 win over the Red Sox, a game played at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Bregman didn’t waste any time Sunday, either.
item.content:encoded:
Last Sunday, Alex Bregman was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch in Cincinnati. He suffered facial fractures and missed three games.
Bregman came back Friday as the DH and Sunday, just a bit over exactly one week since that accident, he hit two home runs and also singled, doubled and walked. His 4-for-4 afternoon led the Cubs to a 4-2 Game 162 win over the Red Sox, a game played at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.
Bregman didn’t waste any time Sunday, either. Pete Crow-Armstrong led off the game with a single and then departed for pinch-runner Tyrone Taylor.
That was great to see. Bregman seemed totally locked in from the moment he stepped into the batter’s box. And that ball was crushed! [VIDEO].
Shōta Imanaga started for the Cubs and threw just the first inning, allowing a home run to Adley Rutschman. That was the 35th homer off Imanaga this year, second-most in MLB this year to Aaron Nola’s 37. Imanaga threw only 12 pitches in this game, which theoretically leaves him available to pitch in the Wild Card Series, maybe Thursday or perhaps even Wednesday. Apart from the homer, Imanaga struck out the other three hitters he faced.
Braxton Garrett, who the Cubs acquired from the Marlins at the trade deadline for minor leaguers Jonathon Long and Jace Beck and who’d been at Triple-A Iowa since, was recalled for this game and went into the game as the “bulk guy” and threw very well. Garrett threw five innings and allowed four hits and a run, though he did issue three walks. He threw 70 pitches and will be in the mix for a starting rotation spot next year.
Bregman drove in all four Cubs runs in this game and finishes with 93 RBI on the season. It’s so good to see him productive after that freak injury. Even if he is limited to DH duty for the Wild Card Series, as noted on the Marquee broadcast, he’s been the Cubs’ second-best hitter (behind PCA) all year and they are going to need that hitting. I noticed that Bregman was wearing a double-flap helmet on the basepaths, though as you can see, not when he hit the home runs.
BCB’s JohnW53 has this fact about Bregman’s two-homer afternoon:
Today’s game was Alex Bregman’s fifth of the season with multiple home runs. Pete Crow-Armstrong has seven such games; Dansby Swanson, three; and Michael Conforto, one, for a total of 16.
The Cubs had a team-record 20 such games last year. They had 19 in 2019, 18 in 1998 and 2004, and 17 in 1930 and 1958. They also had 16 in 2021.
Going into today, the Astros had 16 this year, second to the Rockies’ 18. The Padres had 15.
The Cubs flashed some glove while Garrett was in the game. Here’s a nice stop by Matt Shaw in the fifth [VIDEO].
Jacob Webb succeeded Garrett in the seventh inning and retired all three hitters he faced on just 10 pitches. I don’t think I have to tell you how important it would be if Webb could recover the form that got him 24 straight scoreless appearances before the big meltdown he had at the end of August in Seattle and Arizona.
Colin Rea entered to throw the eighth inning and also retired the Red Sox in order, on just six pitches.
The Cubs then put the game away with a three-run ninth. Miguel Amaya led off with a single and went to third on a single by Taylor. That brought up Bregman, and he came through yet again with this RBI double [VIDEO].
Fact about Bregman’s game from John:
Bregman is just the sixth Cub to hit multiple homers and also have at least one double, one single and one walk. He is the first to do so on the road.
Pete Crow-Armstrong did it in on Aug. 17 in the Cubs’ 10-inning, 7-5 win at home over the White Sox, with his second homer walking it off.
The four others:
Hank Sauer: May 2, 1954, in an 18-10, eight-inning loss to the Pirates
Ryne Sandberg: Aug. 10, 1989, in a 16-13 loss to the Phillies
Corey Patterson: Sept. 7, 2004, in a 7-6, 12-inning loss to the Expos
Chris Coghlan: Sept. 20, 2014, in an 8-7 win over the Dodgers
All had two homers, one double, one single and one walk.
Taylor stopped at third on Bregman’s double, but he then scored on this sac fly by Gabriel Arias [VIDEO].
As mentioned on the Marquee broadcast, Arias is a very good bench player. He can play all infield positions and his bat plays well enough, a really useful guy to have around. That made it 5-2. Ian Happ then struck out, but Michael Conforto doubled, scoring Bregman to give the Cubs a four-run lead [VIDEO].
Rea remained in the game in the ninth to finish up, and he recorded his second save. Here’s the final out [VIDEO].
In other postseason-related news, the Phillies won Sunday and so they take the final wild card spot and will face the Braves in Atlanta in another Wild Card Series beginning Tuesday. The Rangers lost to the Twins, which clinched the A.L. West title for the Astros (who are leading the A’s late and likely will finish 81-81). Houston will host the White Sox in a Wild Card Series starting Tuesday.
One more game note from John:
The Cubs’ six runs made their final total 850, their fourth most in the Modern Era, which began in 1901. They scored 998 in 1930, 982 in 1929 and 855 in 2008. They played 156 games in the first two seasons and 161 in the last.
And for whatever it’s worth, the win gave the Cubs an 89-73 record to the Red Sox’ 87-75. That means that if, somehow, those two clubs meet in the World Series, the Cubs would have home field. The Cubs have the better record over four of the six American League postseason teams; only the Rays and Yankees are better.
So the Cubs will now head to San Diego to begin their own Wild Card Series against the Padres Tuesday evening. I’ll have lots to say about that over the next couple of days here, of course. Michael King has been announced as the Padres starter, but no Cubs starter has yet been named. It could be Matthew Boyd, who’d be going on normal rest, as he last pitched on Thursday against the Marlins at Wrigley Field.
Game time Tuesday is late, so get rested up! 9 p.m. CT, with the game on NBC Sports Network (cable) and streaming on Peacock.
Go Cubs!

item.title: [WMTV 15 NEWS] Misiorowski continues Cy Young Award push and Turang gets 100th RBI as Brewers beat Cardinals 6-4
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: MILWAUKEE (AP) — Jacob Misiorowski allowed two hits in 5 1/3 shutout innings to cap his brilliant season as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the St. Louis Cardinals 6-4 on Sunday. The Brewers improved to 103-59 and closed the regular season with five straight victories, matching their longest streak of the season. The Brewers’ 103 wins broke the franchise record they had set a year earlier when they went 97-65. Milwaukee has home-field advantage throughout the postseason as it gears up for its eig
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — Jacob Misiorowski allowed two hits in 5 1/3 shutout innings to cap his brilliant season as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the St. Louis Cardinals 6-4 on Sunday.
The Brewers improved to 103-59 and closed the regular season with five straight victories, matching their longest streak of the season. The Brewers’ 103 wins broke the franchise record they had set a year earlier when they went 97-65.
Milwaukee has home-field advantage throughout the postseason as it gears up for its eighth playoff appearance in nine years.
St. Louis closed a fourth straight non-playoff season with a 77-85 record, one game worse than the Cardinals’ finish last year.
Misiorowski (16-5) struck out five and walked two while improving his ERA to 1.80, the best in the majors. Misiorowski also has an MLB-leading 252 strikeouts.
Milwaukee gave Misiorowski an early 3-0 lead when Cardinals starter Andre Pallante allowed singles to six of the first seven batters he faced. Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang and Christian Yelich each hit an RBI single.
Turang’s infield hit brought home Jake Bauers for his 100th RBI of the season. Six of them came during this weekend sweep.
Turang became the eighth player in Brewers history to have at least 100 runs and 100 RBIs in a season. Ryan Braun accomplished the feat four times. Robin Yount, Cecil Cooper and Prince Fielder did it twice each. The others are Jeromy Burnitz and John Jaha.
Gary Sánchez hit a two-run homer in the third and Chourio added a two-out RBI single in the fourth to extend the lead to 6-0. Chourio went 3 for 4.
St. Louis scored all four of its runs in the eighth inning off Chad Patrick. Leo Bernal highlighted that outburst with a three-run homer.
Shane Drohan retired the side in order in the ninth to earn his second save.
Pallante (12-9) allowed six runs and 10 hits in five innings.
Up next
The NL Central champion Brewers will host either the Chicago Cubs or San Diego Padres in the opening game of an NL Division Series on Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are set to play their final game of the season on Sunday. They will play the Cincinnati Reds at the Rogers Centre at 3:07 p.m. EDT.
The Blue Jays have announced their lineup for Sunday's game, and it involves a notable decision involving designated hitter George Springer, who is set to be a free agent at the end of this season.
Toronto Blue Jays Make George Springer Decision Before Reds Series Finale
Springer will bat leadoff as the designated hitter for Toronto today. He hasn't been a leadoff hitter for Toronto lately, but he has been a leadoff hitter for much of his career. Sunday's game could be the last of his MLB career. MLB.com's Keegan Matheson wrote on X: In the final game of his #BlueJays contract and what could be the final game of his career, George Springer is batting leadoff.
Springer has hit .248/.320/.402 with15 home runs and 54 RBI this year. Springer played for the Astros from 2014-20. He signed a six-year deal with the Blue Jays after the 2020 season. In his 13-year MLB career, Springer has posted 42.7 bWAR and an .822 OPS with 308 home runs. He is a four-time All-Star, three-time Silver Slugger and a World Series MVP.

On Sunday, the Atlanta Braves will finish the 2026 regular season when they play the Miami Marlins in Florida.
The Braves most recently won by a score of 8-3 on Saturday.
Ronald Acuña Jr. had one strikeout and no hits.
Atlanta Braves Make Ronald Acuña Jr. Decision
Ahead of Sunday’s game, the Braves announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Braves 9/27 M. Dubón LF O. Albies 2B M. Olson 1B A. Riley 3B M. Yastrzemski DH S. Murphy C H. Kim SS B. Hicklen RF D. Keirsey Jr. CF J. Ritchie SP”
Acuña Jr. has been removed from the lineup on Sunday.
The former MVP comes into the day batting .255 with 104 hits, 20 home runs, 55 RBIs, 61 runs and 21 stolen bases in 107 games.
He is in the middle of his 9th MLB season (all with the Braves).
Social Media Reacts To Lineup
Here’s what people were saying about the team’s lineup on Sunday:
@BravesStats: “I’ll be honest: I LOVE seeing Riley batting cleanup here. That’s where he should be. Let’s hope he has a multi-hit day, gets homer #20, and carries good vibes into the postseason.”
@BigWilks23: “One at bat for Olson and get him out of there.”
@meandmyJs: “Def losing the the last game of the reg season! Ughh”
@BALDWIN4MVP: “Type of Lineup in the middle of the 2024-25 season”
Looking At The Braves
The Braves have already clinched a spot in the 2026 MLB playoffs, as they won the National League East division title.
After missing the 2025 MLB playoffs, they look like a true contender to win the World Series this year.
Mark Bowman of MLB.com wrote: “Phillies game moved up to 2:30 pm ET. The Phillies will be the Braves’ WC Series opponent unless they lose to the Rays AND the D-backs beat the Padres today. If the Phillies lose and the D-backs win today, the D-backs have the tiebreaker and thus would be the Braves’ WC Series opponent”

item.title: [FanSided] Ronald Acuña Jr. quietly just gave baseball another reason to fear the Braves

item.content:encoded:
At some point, you’ve probably heard the one about the guy who walks into a doctor’s office, or the horse who walks into a bar. In the case of Atlanta Braves superstar outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr., his story involves the man who walks into the batter’s box, subtly changes his stance and catches fire ahead of the playoffs.
As Major League Baseball’s Mark Bowman recently pointed out, the 2023 NL MVP made a slight tweak to his hitting approach late last month. Mired in a prolonged slump following two hamstring strains, Acuña Jr. did not play in an Aug. 27 win over the eventual NL West champion Dodgers.
Later that night, Acuña Jr. told Braves assistant coach Eddie Pérez he wanted to take early batting practice the next day. During said session, the five-time All-Star closed his stance and, according to Bowman, "backed off the plate a couple of inches [and] separated his feet another few inches.”
The results? Let’s just say the rest of Major League Baseball should be on high alert.
How Atlanta Braves superstar Ronald Acuña Jr. changed his stance and turned his season around
Entering play Sunday, Acuña Jr. is hitting .337 with seven home runs, 20 RBI and a .997 OPS in 112 plate appearances since returning to the lineup on Aug. 28. His batting average has skyrocketed from .235 to .255, and his OPS went from .748 to .796 in less than a month.
If you extrapolate those stats over a full season, Acuña Jr. would finish with 44 home runs, 37 doubles and 125 RBI. Here’s where things get especially interesting: Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez is considered the consensus AL MVP favorite, and he woke up Sunday hitting .316 with 42 home runs, 105 RBI and a 1.036 OPS.
But wait, you say. Acuña Jr. plays in the National League, so how would those numbers compare to Cubs star outfielder and MVP shoo-in Pete Crow-Armstrong? Great question. Crow-Armstrong entered Sunday hitting .278 with 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 31 doubles, 41 steals and a .941 OPS. In that case, we’re not sure whether PCA would be running away with the NL MVP.
“When he is healthy and he gets on one of these streaks, he’s one of the best players in baseball,” said Ozzie Albies, who has played with Acuña since the latter’s 2018 debut. “There's nothing else to say about that.”
Arguably the most remarkable part is how Acuña Jr. responded to sitting during a playoff race. Keep in mind the Braves only had a five-game NL East lead over the Phillies when the veteran outfielder rejoined the lineup on Aug. 28. But rather than complain or take things personally, Acuña Jr. took it upon himself to fix what wasn’t working.
Fans and observers can say whatever they want about Acuña Jr., who has frequently drawn pushback for his enthusiasm, celebrations and durability. But he was injured during the Braves’ 2021 title run, and he’s still chasing his first World Series plate appearance. He turns 29 in December and only has two years of team control left; time is running out for him to guarantee himself a nine-figure contract.
But if Acuña Jr. continues to hit how he has of late, the only question is whether he’ll clear $250 million on his next deal. Guiding the Braves to their second championship in six years would go a long way in convincing ownership he’s still worth the risk.

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are heading into game 162 of the MLB regular season with their tails between their legs. They will play their final game against the Cincinnati Reds, instead of moving through the playoffs with a World Series Title in sight. The Toronto Blue Jays news of the day involves Brandon Valenzuela.
The final game of the year, on Sunday, September 27th, 2026, will be broadcast at 1:07 PM Mountain Time, 3:07 PM Eastern Time. Max Scherzer will take the mound one last time, going against Brandon Williamson.
Toronto Blue Jays fans can tune in to Sportsnet, TVA Sports, and on the radio on SN590 THE FAN.
Toronto Blue Jays Announce Final Brandon Valenzuela Decision For Last Game Against The Cincinnati Reds
Before the first pitch of the final game of the 2026 season, the Blue Jays announced a final decision on Valenzuela.
This is the lineup that the Blue Jays announced for their final game:
- DH: George Springer
- RF: Brett Bateman
- 3B: Kazuma Okamoto
- 1B: Charles McAdoo
- LF: Davis Schneider
- C: Brandon Valenzuela
- CF: Myles Straw
- SS: Andres Gimenez
- 2B: Ernie Clement
Starting Pitcher: Max Scherzer
As you can see from the Blue Jays announcement, Alejandro Kirk has been replaced by Valenzuela for Sunday’s final game. It will be the 25-year-old‘s 91st game of the year.
Additionally, George Springer, Charles McAdoo, Davis Schneider, and Myles Straw are also coming into the lineup. Coming out in their place are Nathan Lukes, Sean Keys, and Josh Smith.
Looking At Brandon Valenzuela & Alejandro Kirk
Valenzuela has been a solid contributor for the Blue Jays this season.
The young catcher has recorded 53 hits, 22 RBIs, two stolen bases, nine doubles, 28 walks, and eight home runs in 90 games. He started 83 games at catcher and five games at first base.
On the other hand, Kirk has been one of the bright spots of the Blue Jays’ otherwise down year.
In 79 games, the 27-year-old recorded 77 hits, eight doubles, 43 RBIs, one stolen base, 33 walks, and 10 home runs.
Brandon Valenzuela’s Future With The Toronto Blue Jays
Valenzuela’s future with the Blue Jays is uncertain.
However, if Springer moves on from Toronto, there will be room for Valenzuela. Kirk has been a better hitter than Valenzuela, making him an easy choice to slide into the designated hitter role. However, if Valenzuela improves his swing, he could spend some games at DH, too.
Valenzuela has pre-arbitration for two years after earning $734,096 in 2026.
One way or another, Valenzuela will be an active member of the Blue Jays for at least another year.

item.title: [That Balls Outta Here] Rival scout underscores Bryce Harper's playoff pressure as Phillies collapse looms
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies need a win or an Arizona Diamondbacks loss today to clinch a Wild Card spot in the National League on the regular season's final day. So how did they get here? Well, the Phillies have lost four games in a row and have been outscored 23-3 during this span. They had a 6.5 game lead over the Diamondbacks on Sept. 1, but have gone just 9-14 this month. If the Phillies miss out on the postseason, it will be an epic collapse.
Luckily, Zack Wheeler is taking the mound against the Tampa Bay Rays in a must-win game, so the Phillies have a pretty good shot of clinching a Wild Card berth on Sunday. And if they do so, their superstar player, Bryce Harper, will have a ton of pressure on him this October, according to one rival scout.
Why this postseason means more for Phillies' Bryce Harper
It appears that Harper will be ticketed for the Baseball Hall of Fame when all is said and done and the book is closed on his illustrious career. However, the 33-year-old still has never won a championship in his 15-year MLB tenure.
"Bryce Harper needs a title to complete his resume," one rival NL scout said. "Not sure anyone else has more pressure in regards to their legacy. They have had stacked teams in Philly and the everyday fans know that the Nationals won (a title) after he left."
Harper and the Phillies got close to winning a title in 2022, which saw them lose to the Houston Astros in six games. Harper had his biggest postseason moment with a go-ahead home run against the San Diego Padres in the NLCS, lifting the Phillies to the NL pennant. But the Phillies ultimately came up short in '22 and then again in 2023 when they lost in the NLCS to the Diamondbacks. The Phillies haven't made it past the NLDS since then despite making the playoffs the last two years.
As previously alluded to, the Washington Nationals won the World Series in 2019, which was the same year that Harper left in free agency to sign a 13-year, $330 million deal with the Phillies. As impressive as Harper's career in the majors has been, he still needs to win a title to stamp his legacy as one of the all-time great players.
For that, no one has more pressure on them to perform this postseason. The Phillies need to make it there first, but if they do, Harper must step up and lead his team on a deep run in October.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Why Ben Rice's MVP case deserves more love in a lost Aaron Judge season
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: Without Aaron Judge for most of the season, the AL MVP race is wide open. The favorite for much of the year has been Houston Astros slugger Yordan Álvarez, but he's far from a sure thing. The New York Yankees have seen Cam Schlittler's candidacy get more recognition in recent weeks, but there's another Yankee who's being grossly overlooked. item.content:encoded:
Without Aaron Judge for most of the season, the AL MVP race is wide open. The favorite for much of the year has been Houston Astros slugger Yordan Álvarez, but he's far from a sure thing. The New York Yankees have seen Cam Schlittler's candidacy get more recognition in recent weeks, but there's another Yankee who's being grossly overlooked.
Ben Rice was obviously a breakout star for New York last season, but this year he has reached a new gear. Aaron Boone predicted that Rice would clock 39 dingers this season, which was the total the Dartmouth product was sitting on when the Yankees took on the Tampa Bay Rays on September 23, with five games left to play. Neither team had anything left to play for with playoff positions solidified, so it seemed like a good chance that Rice would finish at that number.
But just like that, the 27-year-old bested his manager when he led off the bottom of the first with a solo shot. That wasn't all, though, as Rice came back up to the plate to lead off the bottom of the fourth and smacked his second tater of the game. He now sits at 41 homers and enters the Yankees' record book as a result.
His 40th blast of the year put him in some elite company in franchise history. Rice became just the eighth Yankee to hit 40 or more homers in a season at age 27 or younger. The rest of the list includes four inner-circle Hall of Famers: Babe Ruth (twice), Lou Gehrig (twice), Mickey Mantle (twice), and Joe DiMaggio. In addition to those four, the other three are former single-season home run king Roger Maris, Juan Soto, and, of course, Judge.
Ben Rice's 40th homer underscores how incredibly valuable he's been to the Yankees in Aaron Judge's absence
MLB.com's latest awards poll has Rice as a distant fifth in the voting, behind Álvarez, Junior Caminero, Bobby Witt Jr., and Schlittler, in that order. There are a few things that don't make much sense here.
Álvarez has been great this year, but there's a narrative among some that he's been Judge-like that just isn't true. Air Yordan has posted a 181 wRC+ through September 23, which is still over 20 points lower than Judge's 203 mark last season, which also happened to be the lowest wRC+ he has put up in any of his three MVP campaigns. That's relevant because he is seeking to become the first full-time DH to take home the honor other than Shohei Ohtani.
As for Caminero, he began generating a lot of MVP buzz with his two walk-off homers in mid-September, as if those wins somehow count more than victories at any other point during the season. More importantly, Rice has caught up to him, as both now have 41 homers. Rice has also surpassed him in on-base percentage (.362 versus .360) and slugging percentage (.537 versus .523).
The DH argument also works against Rice, but only to an extent. He's played 55 games at first base and has mostly ceded playing time in the field to accommodate trade deadline acquisition Luis Garcia Jr. It should also be noted that Caminero isn't a great defensive third baseman and is last among qualifiers at the position with -11 outs above average.
More importantly, there's the Judge factor in all of this. The Astros are on the brink of either missing the playoffs for the second year in a row or winning the most pathetic division in MLB history, dipping under .500 late in the campaign. The Rays have had their big boppers like Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda healthy for most of the year.
Losing a player as singular as Judge is a huge blow to a team, but the Yankees are playoff-bound yet again. Throw in a lengthy absence from Cody Bellinger and the fact that they're starting to print milk cartons with Giancarlo Stanton's face on them, and it's been Rice who has kept the offense afloat all year.
If the point of this exercise is to recognize the player who has been the most valuable, then the loss of Judge looms large. We've had our frustrations, but the Yankees really haven't skipped a beat without Judge and his enormous value. Rice is a big reason why, and while it might not be enough to win him the award, he should be a much larger part of the conversation.

item.content:encoded:
Pirates’ Nick Gonzales Positioned to End Year in Exclusive Group of .300 Hitters
Only seven players enter the final day of the 2026 season with a batting average of .300 or better. Pirates infielder Nick Gonzales (.302) is one of them.
Gonzales has a chance to be the first qualified hitter for the Pirates to finish with a batting average of .300 or better since teammate Bryan Reynolds hit .302 in 2021.
While accomplishing the feat would be “cool,” Gonzales is not stepping into the batter’s box thinking about his batting average.
“You just try to be consistent every single day and if that’s where I am, that’s where I am,” he explained. “It’s something that could really eat you up if you really focus on it too much throughout the year. I just play my game and try to be consistent.”
Batting average is considered to be an antiquated stat by some in today’s game. Given Gonzales’ profile and background, he’s someone who sees the value in hitting for average.
“I think it’s still a testament to finding ways to get hits,” he said. “I’m not a guy who’s gonna just swing for home runs. That’s not really my game. So, you gotta kinda learn how to find hits.”
The six other qualified hitters who join Gonzales in the .300 club are the Astros’ Yordan Alvarez (.316), Diamondbacks’ Gabriel Moreno (.311), Phillies’ Luis Arraez (.310), Rays Chandler Simpson (.306), Marlins’ Otto Lopez (.305) and Rockies’ TJ Rumfield (.300).
10 years ago, 25 hitters finished with a .300 batting average. The fact now that so few hitters are able to finish at or above the mark is a testament to the quality of pitchers in today’s game, Gonzales believes.
“I don’t think hitters are worse,” he said. “I think it’s just that the pitching is that good.”
Gonzales’ offensive showing with the Pirates this season has been the best of his career. But while his offense has been a bright spot this season, his defense has lagged well behind.
Gonzales, a natural second baseman, has been tasked with manning a new position. After adding Brandon Lowe at second base in the offseason, the Pirates had to shift Gonzales to third base. The 27-year-old has committed 11 errors in 112 games at the hot corner with minus-15 defensive runs saved.
While Gonzales hasn’t had the year he’s wanted defensively, he’s not allowed his fielding woes to carry over to the plate.
“You don’t take your glove to hit and you don’t take your bat to play defense. So, just flush it. Forget about it,” he explained. “As soon as I step back in the box, it’s over with.”
Through all of the defensive inconsistencies this season, Gonzales has remained a steady presence in the Pirates’ lineup. Finishing the season in what will be an exclusive group of players with a .300 batting average would be a reflection of the progress he’s made offensively this season.
“He should take pride in that, in how he’s been able to swing the bat for us,” said manager Don Kelly. “He’s had some huge at-bats and swung the bat well. He’s been a big part of our offensive success this year.”
More about:Pirates

item.content:encoded:
Sep 27, 2026, 11:30 AM ET
New York Mets outfielder Juan Soto (hand) is starting in left field and will bat second for the 2026 season finale on Sunday against the division-rival Washington Nationals and left-hander DJ Herz, according to MLB.com. The Mets pulled Soto from Saturday's game early in D.C. after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch in the ninth inning, but thankfully, X-rays on his hand came back negative. The 27-year-old Dominican enters the final game of the season with only 395 at-bats in 2026 thanks to two separate trips to the injured list with calf injuries. When on the field for the Mets, though, the five-time All-Star continued to produce, slashing .278/.397/.522 with a .919 OPS, 27 home runs, 68 RBI, 63 runs scored, and nine stolen bases across 110 games and 477 plate appearances. Soto enters Sunday's contest with a .266 (25-for-94) average with five home runs and 14 RBI in 23 games played in the final month of the regular season. With better health next year, Soto is hoping that he can help get the Mets back into the postseason.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
More Recent News
Kade Anderson Suffers Forearm Contusion on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:23 AM ET
Seattle Mariners rookie left-hander Kade Anderson (forearm) had X-rays come back negative after he was hit by a comebacker on his left forearm in his start on Saturday against the division-rival Los Angeles Angels, according to Daniel Kramer of MLB.com. Anderson and the Mariners avoided a significant scare in Anderson's final start of what has been a stellar debut season in the professional ranks. Before leaving after 3 1/3 innings of work at T-Mobile Park, Anderson did not allow a run on four hits while walking just one and striking out four to lower his season ERA to 3.79. The 22-year-old former third overall pick from LSU was as dominant as they come in the minors in 2026 before being called up to join Seattle's big-league starting rotation late in the year. In his seven starts for the M's, Anderson went 2-2 with a 3.79 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, and 32 strikeouts in 35 2/3 innings pitched. He dominated at Double-A Arkansas, posting a 1.06 ERA, 0.64 WHIP, and 135:13 K:BB in 18 starts over 93 1/3 frames. Anderson is one of the best young arms in all of baseball and should have a rotation spot locked up to begin the 2027 campaign.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Daniel Kramer
Jesus Luzardo Being Activated, Will be Available on Sunday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:17 AM ET
The Philadelphia Phillies will activate left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder) from the 15-day injured list on Sunday for the regular-season finale in a must-win game, interim manager Don Mattingly told Matt Gelb of The Athletic. Luzardo will be available out of the bullpen. The Phillies will have all hands on deck as they try to beat the Tampa Bay Rays to punch their ticket to the postseason as the final Wild-Card team in the National League. The 28-year-old Luzardo had been one of the best pitchers in baseball this year before landing on the IL with inflammation in his left shoulder back on Sept. 12. The native of Peru is returning to a 14-5 record, 2.87 ERA (2.78 FIP), a 1.08 WHIP, and a 221:52 K:BB in 178 2/3 innings pitched and 29 starts in his second season with the Phillies. Luzardo's strong 2026 campaign on the mound earned him his first career trip to the All-Star Game. If he is used in Sunday's game against Tampa, it could rule Luzardo out of starting a game in the Wild-Card series next week if the Phillies advance.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Matt Gelb
Griffin Jax Suffers Back Contusion on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:07 AM ET
The Tampa Bay Rays are saying that right-hander Griffin Jax (back) was removed from his appearance in Saturday's win over the Philadelphia Phillies due to a lower-back contusion, according to the Tampa Bay Times' Marc Topkin. Jax only made it three innings during his start at Citizens Bank Park, but he did not allow a run while giving up only two hits, walking none, and striking out one batter to lower his season ERA to 3.53. The 31-year-old veteran took a 104 mph liner off the bat of shortstop Trea Turner off his back in the third inning, and the Rays were not going to take any chances with Griffin. Manager Kevin Cash and Jax said after the game that he is not expected to miss any time, which means he should be available for the start of the American League Division Series against an undetermined opponent on Oct. 3. Jax finishes his first full season in Tampa with an 8-10 record, 3.53 ERA (3.76 FIP) and 1.17 WHIP with a career-high 116 strikeouts and 35 walks in 112 1/3 innings across 34 outings (23 starts). He began the 2026 season as Tampa's primary ninth-inning arm before making a successful transition to the rotation.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tampa Bay Times - Marc Topkin
Chandler Simpson Unlikely to Play Until ALDS


Keith Hernandez




Sep 27, 2026, 11:00 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (foot) said on Saturday afternoon that his right foot was "just a little sore" from Friday's foul ball, according to Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times. Simpson did not play in the team's win over the Philadelphia Phillies on Saturday and likely will not play in the regular-season finale on Sunday "to take precautions." He is fully confident that he will be good to go for the American League Division Series opener on Oct. 3. The Rays pulled the 25-year-old speedster from Friday's game early after he fouled a ball off his foot in the sixth inning. Simpson will end his 2026 season with a strong .306/.333/.356 slash line with a .689 OPS, zero home runs, 38 RBI, a league-leading 46 stolen bases, and 66 runs scored in 151 games played across 612 plate appearances in only his second season in the majors. Hopefully for the Rays, Simpson's foot injury does not impact his ability to run once the ALDS kicks off late next week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tampa Bay Times - Marc Topkin
Chandler Simpson Sitting Out With Foot Injury


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 6:58 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (foot) is not in the team's starting lineup for Saturday's game in Philadelphia against the Phillies, per MLB.com. Victor Mesa Jr. is starting in left field for the Rays and is batting fifth against Phillies right-hander Aaron Nola. The Rays are being cautious with the speedster, giving him a day off in Game 2 of the series at Citizens Bank Park after Simpson fouled a ball off his right foot during the win on Friday night. The Rays already have a first-round bye locked up in the American League, so Simpson will have plenty of time to heal before the start of the AL Division Series. If the 25-year-old does not play in the regular-season finale on Sunday, he will finish his second big-league season in 2026 with a very nice .306/.333/.356 slash line, .689 OPS, zero home runs, 38 RBI, and 66 runs scored across 151 games and 612 plate appearances. Simpson has no power to speak of, but he leads the league with 46 stolen bases after swiping 44 bags as a rookie in 2025. His speed in the outfield and on the basepaths is a game-changer for the first-place Rays.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Juan Soto Hit by Pitch on his Hand, X-Rays Come Back Negative


Keith Hernandez




Sep 26, 2026, 5:28 PM ET
New York Mets superstar outfielder Juan Soto (hand) left Saturday's game against the division-rival Washington Nationals early after being hit on the right hand by a 91.7 mph sinker, according to Anthony DiComo of MLB.com. Soto was in some clear discomfort, but X-rays on his hand came back negative. Before leaving the game, Soto went 2-for-4 at the plate with a strikeout. He was replaced in left field by Nick Morabito. It sounds like Soto avoided a serious injury, but with just one more game in the 2026 regular season, the Mets might hold the left-handed slugger out to close out another disappointing season for the Mets. The 27-year-old five-time All-Star and six-time Silver Slugger winner missed extended time this year with two separate calf injuries, but he still came into Saturday's contest with a solid .276/.395/.522 slash line, .917 OPS, 27 home runs, 68 RBI, 63 runs scored, and nine stolen bases across his 391 at-bats. With better health in 2027, Soto could quickly get back to elite five-category production for his fantasy managers.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Anthony DiComo
Kyle Stowers is Battling an Abdominal Injury


Dave Funnell




Sep 26, 2026, 2:09 PM ET
Miami Marlins outfielder Kyle Stowers (abdomen) is out of the lineup on Saturday due to an abdominal injury. The 28-year-old has been battling through injuries all season long, and this latest ailment comes on the heels of his absence from Friday's lineup. It's unclear how serious the issue is at this time, but with only two games remaining in the season, it's quite possible that he has already played his last game of 2026. Fantasy baseball managers would be wise to stay updated with Sunday's lineup to see if he can return for one final game this year. Despite missing time earlier in the season, Stowers has still managed to hit 21 home runs, albeit with a discouraging .239 batting average. Should he be able to return healthy to start next season, he could be a sleeper pick in some drafts due to his power upside and dual eligibility, as he also qualifies at first base.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller

Dave Funnell




Sep 26, 2026, 1:53 PM ET
Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Jack Flaherty (forearm) is set to be activated from the 60-Day Injured List on Sunday and start for the Tigers in their season finale. The 30-year-old last pitched on July 20 and has been out of action recovering and rehabbing ever since. He has made just two rehab appearances, striking out five batters over 3.2 scoreless innings across various minor league levels. He also tossed a two-inning simulated game last week, giving the Tigers enough confidence to put him on the mound for the final day of the regular season. Should he pitch effectively without any setbacks, this would be a good "peace-of-mind" way to finish the year and head into a normal offseason. Xavier Edwards Still Out of Marlins Lineup

It's unclear if he will return at all this season, and with just one game remaining on the schedule, he very well may have played his last game. Dave Funnell

However, the 30-year-old also expects to have a relatively normal offseason, hopefully alleviating any long-term concerns about a major injury. With surgery currently off the table, the belief is that time away from throwing will give his shoulder what it needs to return to full health. With the expectation that he will be ready for Opening Day in 2027, he is someone to remember at the top end of drafts come draft day, as his track record for endurance is unparalleled. He will miss time while he heals, ending his 2026 season on a sour note. Still, despite battling multiple injuries all season, he will finish with a .299 batting average and 12 home runs over 104 games. While nothing has been confirmed, it would appear that he will be ready for Spring Training next season. Elmer Rodriguez to Pitch on Sunday for Yankees

Sep 26, 2026, 12:47 PM ET
New York Yankees right-handed pitching prospect Elmer Rodriguez will pitch on Sunday against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles in the final game of the 2026 regular season, weather permitting, according to Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. It will be Rodriguez's seventh start in his first year in the big leagues, and his first since he allowed four earned runs in 3 2/3 innings with three walks and five strikeouts in a loss to the Los Angeles Angels on the road on Aug. 31. Rodriguez is the team's No. 2 overall prospect, per MLB Pipeline, but his lack of control at the major-league level in a small sample size will make him extremely risky for fantasy managers still vying for a championship on the final weekend of the regular season.--Keith Hernandez

(AP) — Yordan Alvarez launched a three-run homer and the Houston Astros went deep five times Saturday night as they moved closer to a division title with a 13-2 victory over the Athletics. item.content:encoded:
WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — Yordan Alvarez launched a three-run homer and the Houston Astros went deep five times Saturday night as they moved closer to a division title with a 13-2 victory over the Athletics.
Houston (80-81) can clinch the AL West crown and the No. 3 seed in the American League playoffs with another win Sunday over the A’s in their regular-season finale or a Texas Rangers loss at Minnesota. Either team will become the first to win a division with a .500 record or worse, excluding shortened seasons.
Alvarez homered in the fifth inning to put the Astros up 6-1. His 42nd homer of the season tied him with Tampa Bay slugger Junior Caminero for second in the AL.
Houston finished with 16 hits as Jeremy Peña, Isaac Paredes and Jose Altuve combined for nine of them and seven RBIs.
Peña hit a pair of two-run homers, one in the third and the other in the eighth. He finished 4 for 6 with four RBIs. Parades homered in the first to open the scoring and went 3 for 5.
Hayden Wesneski (6-2) threw seven innings and struck out five while allowing six hits and two runs.
The Astros scored six runs, including Lucas Spence’s solo homer, between the seventh and ninth to expand their lead to 13-2.
Jack Perkins (3-13) pitched five innings for the Athletics. He struck out nine but gave up six runs and three homers.
Up next
Neither team had announced a starting pitcher for Sunday’s regular-season finale.
___

item.title: [Field Level Media] Orioles' Pete Alonso looks to play all 162 games again in finale vs. Yankees
item.description: A majority of the focus for the New York Yankees is planning their roster and preparing to host the Boston Red Sox in next week’s wild-card series. Another area of focus will be finishing out the regular season with their 94th win when the Yankees host the Baltimore Orioles on Sunday, weather permitting. The start time has been moved up to 1:05 p.m. The Yankees (93-68) were off on Saturday because a nor’easter resulted in a single-admission doubleheader on Friday. Since New York was eliminated f
item.content:encoded:
A majority of the focus for the New York Yankees is planning their roster and preparing to host the Boston Red Sox in next week’s wild-card series.
Another area of focus will be finishing out the regular season with their 94th win when the Yankees host the Baltimore Orioles on Sunday, weather permitting.
The start time has been moved up to 1:05 p.m.
The Yankees (93-68) were off on Saturday because a nor’easter resulted in a single-admission doubleheader on Friday. Since New York was eliminated from the American League East race on Tuesday night, its past four games have seen the team give regulars time off and rest some of its prominent relievers while seeing other defensive alignments.
On Friday, the Yankees took a 10-2 loss in the opener and earned their fifth doubleheader split of the season with a 6-3 victory before the tarp was put on the field immediately after the final pitch.
Cody Bellinger, Luis Garcia Jr. were among those who rested in the opener before starting in the second game. Anthony Volpe played third base in the first game and shortstop in the second game after playing only at second base following his return from the minor leagues on Sept. 10.
Volpe had three hits in the doubleheader, including a two-run double in the sixth inning Friday night. Volpe’s newfound versatility may be something for the Yankees to consider for their postseason roster as he’s hitting .265 (11 for 49) with nine RBIs in 14 games since returning.
“This is the most important part of the season,” Volpe said. “This is the best part of why you do it; this is why you play. It’s Yankees/Red Sox — that’s what October baseball is.”
Ben Rice had three hits in the doubleheader and enters the regular-season finale with 41 homers and 97 RBIs in a year when Aaron Judge has played 66 games and may miss the wild-card series because of a moderately strained right calf.
The Orioles (79-82) are concluding their second straight losing season after winning 275 games from 2022-2024.
Pete Alonso enters Sunday with 43 homers and 113 RBIs in his first season with the Orioles. He will win the AL RBI title and is one ahead of Yordan Alvarez and Junior Caminero for the AL home run crown.
Alonso is looking to play in his 162nd game of the season for the third consecutive year.
Eight of Alonso’s past 10 hits are homers and he has the most homers by an Oriole since Mark Trumbo mashed 47 in 2016.
“It’s impressive,” manager Craig Albernaz said. “It’s not only the at-bat quality and the pitches he’s getting, he’s not missing them. He’s squaring them up pretty good.”
If the game gets played, the Yankees will get another look at Elmer Rodriguez (0-3, 5.40 ERA). Rodriguez has made six starts this season and has 21 strikeouts and 16 walks in 26 2/3 innings.
Rodriguez last pitched in the major leagues when he struggled through 3 2/3 innings during a 10-1 road loss to the Angels on Aug. 31. He also showed increased velocity Aug. 26 in a no-decision in New York’s 9-3 win over Houston when he allowed three runs on three hits in six innings.
Shane Baz (6-15, 4.11) starts for Baltimore and likely will pitch an abbreviated outing similar to Trevor Rogers, who threw 55 pitches in four innings Friday. Baz is 2-6 with a 4.37 ERA in his past 10 starts and took a no-decision Monday against Toronto when Baltimore rallied in the eighth inning.
Baz is 0-3 with a 6.48 ERA in eight career starts against the Yankees.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Manny Machado hit a three-run homer and the San Diego Padres beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 10-7 on Saturday to secure the No. 4 seed in the National League playoffs.
San Diego will host every game in a best-of-three Wild Card Series against the fifth-seeded Chicago Cubs beginning Tuesday. The winner will face the NL Central champion Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-five Division Series.
The Cubs eliminated the Padres 2-1 in the wild-card round at Chicago last season.
Xander Bogaerts also went deep for the Padres (90-71), who clinched their club-record third straight 90-win season and seventh in team history. They earned their franchise-best third consecutive postseason berth with a 4-2 win Thursday night at the NL West champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Diamondbacks had their six-game winning streak snapped but remain alive for the NL's third wild-card spot. They are one game behind Philadelphia going into Sunday's season finales and hold the tiebreaker. The Phillies lost their fourth straight game, 12-1 to AL East champion Tampa Bay.
Arizona's Gabriel Moreno hit an RBI single and went 1 for 3 with a walk to keep his average at .311, just ahead of injured Phillies infielder Luis Arraez (.310) in the race for the NL batting title.
Moreno's spot in the order came up after Mason Miller loaded the bases with no outs in the ninth, but the Diamondbacks sent pinch-hitter Adrian Del Castillo to the plate and he struck out. Miller allowed three runs.
Machado hit a 1-1 pitch from Jose Cabrera (0-4) into the home run porch in the right-field corner for a 6-4 lead in the fourth. That gave Machado his eighth career 30-homer season, tying Arizona's Nolan Arenado and Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber for the most among active players.
It was his fourth 30-homer season with San Diego, tying Adrian Gonzalez for the most in team history.
The Diamondbacks went ahead 4-3 in the top of the fourth on James McCann's two-run homer to straightaway center off Walker Buehler.
Arizona led 2-1 in the third before the Padres went in front on Ty France's RBI groundout and Gavin Sheets' RBI double that center fielder Tim Tawa lost in the lights and twilight sky.
Bogaerts hit a solo homer in the two-run fifth, and Jake Cronenworth added a two-run single in the sixth.
Yuki Matsui (5-1) got the win in relief.
Up next
Diamondbacks RHP Michael Soroka (9-5, 3.31 ERA) is scheduled to pitch the season finale Sunday. The Padres hadn't announced a starter.

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are one of the few teams still playing for their postseason lives with two days remaining in the regular season.
After losing Friday night in their series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Phillies hold just a one-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks for the final Wild Card spot in the National League, and the D-Backs hold the tiebreaker.
This makes Saturday’s game and potentially Sunday’s game pivotal for the Phillies, who will be without infielder Luis Arraez after he sustained an ankle injury earlier this week.
Phillies Announce Bryce Harper Move
With Arraez out of the lineup, it hurts to lose one of the best pure hitters in the game, but it also gives the Phillies a little more flexibility with how they construct their lineup.
With that, Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly has decided to move Bryce Harper from right field back to first base on Saturday, while Alec Bohm will transition to third and Bryson Stott to second.
Kyle Schwarber will remain the designated hitter, and Trea Turner will stay at shortstop. Taking over in right field for Harper will be Bryan De La Cruz.
Here’s the Phillies’ full starting lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Phillies 9/26 T. Turner SS K. Schwarber DH B. Harper 1B A. Bohm 3B B. Stott 2B B. De La Cruz RF B. Marsh LF J. Realmuto C J. Crawford CF A. Nola SP.”

Looking at Harper and the Phillies
The Phillies enter Saturday with an 87-73 overall record and have gone 4-6 over their last 10 games, with Harper going 3-for-7 at the plate over the last two.
On the season, he’s hitting .270 with 153 hits, 28 home runs, and 86 RBIs while slugging .485 with a .867 OPS.

item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON (AP) — New York Mets left fielder Juan Soto left Saturday’s game against the Washington Nationals after being hit by a pitch on his right hand in the ninth inning.
Manager Andy Green said X-rays were negative. Green said he did not know whether Soto would play in Sunday's season finale.
“He got squared up on his hand pretty good,” Green said.
Soto was hit by Richard Lovelady’s 91 mph sinker and immediately spun around, then began shaking his right hand while walking toward first base. He then turned around, was met by an athletic trainer and returned to the dugout.
Soto is hitting .278 with 27 homers and 68 RBIs in his second season with the Mets. He had two injured list stints this season because of calf strains.

item.content:encoded:
El cuerpo de pitcheo de los Seattle Mariners ha recibido un impacto devastador en el momento más crítico de la campaña. El estelar relevista mexicano Andrés Muñoz ha quedado marginado por lo que resta de la Temporada 2026 de las Grandes Ligas tras sufrir una severa lesión que le impedirá volver al montículo durante la recta final de la fase regular y la inminente postemporada.
La noticia sacudió la cueva del conjunto norteño tras confirmarse los estudios médicos pertinentes, los cuales revelaron una afección de consideración en su brazo de lanzar que requiere reposo absoluto y tratamiento especializado.
PUBLICIDAD
La baja del serpentinero originario de Los Mochis, Sinaloa, representa un contratiempo gigantesco para la reestructuración del bullpen del manejador de Seattle, que pierde a su cerrador estelar y a una de las armas más dominantes en los episodios finales de los encuentros de cara a los playoffs de la MLB.
¿Cuál fue la lesión de Andrés Muñoz y cómo será su rehabilitación?
El relevista azteca, ampliamente reconocido en las Grandes Ligas por su devastadora bola rápida que supera con soltura las 100 millas por hora combinada con un slider letal, venía desempeñando un rol protagónico dentro del esquema defensivo del equipo.
Su incapacidad para continuar en el terreno de juego no solo merma el potencial del cuerpo de lanzadores de los Mariners de cara a sus aspiraciones en Octubre, sino que además frena momentáneamente la que estaba siendo una de las actuaciones individuales más destacadas para un lanzador mexicano en la Gran Carpa.
PUBLICIDAD
Con la confirmación de que no volverá a vestirse de corto en lo que resta de la competencia debido a una inflamación en la rodilla derecha, la prioridad absoluta para el cuerpo médico de los Mariners y para el propio serpentinero se traslada hacia un plan de rehabilitación integral. El objetivo primordial de la organización es garantizar una recuperación anatómica completa sin precipitar los tiempos de retorno, asegurando que el ligamento y los músculos de su brazo de lanzar sanen adecuadamente.
Directivos y especialistas del club han enfatizado que se tomarán todas las precauciones necesarias para que la preparación invernal de Muñoz no sufra contratiempos mayores, con la mirada puesta en que el mexicano pueda presentarse al cien por ciento de sus capacidades físicas para el inicio de los entrenamientos de primavera del próximo año.
PUBLICIDAD
Para la afición mexicana y los seguidores de la Gran Carpa, la baja de Andrés Muñoz representa una ausencia sensible en el escaparate internacional, privando a la pelota tricolor de contar con uno de sus máximos referentes disputando las instancias decisivas de la Serie Mundial. Sin embargo, su sólida labor a lo largo de 2026 deja un precedente claro de su estatus como uno de los relevistas élite de todo el béisbol organizado.
Así había sido el año de Muñoz en el montículo de los Mariners
Antes de este desafortunado percance físico que forzó su paso a la lista de lesionados por el resto del año, Andrés Muñoz firmó una actuación memorable sobre el diamante, consolidándose como uno de los taponeros más confiables y dominantes de la Liga Americana. Sus registros individuales reflejan el peso específico que el sinaloense ejercía cada vez que tomaba la pelota en la novena entrada.
PUBLICIDAD
Durante sus 59.1 entradas lanzadas a lo largo del curso, el “Plebe” acreditó una sensacional efectividad de 2.12, permitiendo muy poco daño a las ofensivas enemigas y manteniendo un control magistral en situaciones de máxima presión. Además, acumuló un total de 24 partidos salvados, asegurando victorias cruciales para la franquicia de la División Oeste.
La capacidad del derecho para abanicar enemigos volvió a quedar en evidencia al registrar 78 ponches, manteniendo un promedio de ponches por cada nueve entradas significativamente superior a la media de la liga. Asimismo, su WHIP (promedio de basquetbolistas embasados por entrada) se mantuvo en un sobresaliente 1.01, demostrando la enorme dificultad que enfrentaron los bateadores rivales para establecerle contacto sólido.
PUBLICIDAD
<br>
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

item.content:encoded:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. consiguió un sencillo productor tan extraño que fue necesaria una repetición en cámara lenta para entenderlo.
Con récord de 0-2 ante el relevista de los Reds Luis Mey, Guerrero golpeó un sinker hacia el centro mientras su bate se rompía.
El barril roto cayó frente al plato y golpeó la pelota por segunda vez, desviándose hacia el lado derecho del infield y permitiendo que entrara una carrera.
Según las reglas de MLB, la jugada continúa cuando una pelota bateada golpea un fragmento del bate roto en territorio bueno. El insólito sencillo ayudó a iniciar una séptima entrada de cuatro carreras para Toronto en su dramática victoria por 6-5.
Pareció un caos absoluto, pero en el box score fue simplemente otra carrera impulsada para Guerrero.

item.title: [marca.com] Vladimir Guerrero Jr. records one of baseball’s weirdest RBI singles
item.dc:creator: Angel Nakamura
item.description: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has produced plenty of memorable hits during his career, but few have looked quite like the one he delivered Friday night against the Reds. The Blue Jays first baseman helped ignite a decisive seventh-inning rally in Toronto's 6-5 victory at Rogers Centre with an RBI single that required a bit of baseball luck, and an unexpected assist from his broken bat. Facing Cincinnati reliever Luis Mey with an 0-2 count, Guerrero swung at a sinker and chopped a ground ball toward the
item.content:encoded:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has produced plenty of memorable hits during his career, but few have looked quite like the one he delivered Friday night against the Reds.
The Blue Jays first baseman helped ignite a decisive seventh-inning rally in Toronto's 6-5 victory at Rogers Centre with an RBI single that required a bit of baseball luck, and an unexpected assist from his broken bat.
Facing Cincinnati reliever Luis Mey with an 0-2 count, Guerrero swung at a sinker and chopped a ground ball toward the middle of the infield. As he made contact, the bat shattered.
Slow-motion replay revealed a remarkable sequence. After the ball initially came off Guerrero's bat, the severed barrel landed several feet in front of home plate and made contact with the baseball a second time. The unexpected deflection altered the ball's path, sending it toward the right side of the infield.

item.content:encoded:
On Saturday, the Philadelphia Phillies will continue their series with the Tampa Bay Rays in Florida.
They are coming off a 2-0 loss on Friday.
Matt Gelb of The Athletic wrote: “Rays 2, Phillies 0. The Phillies have scored two runs in their last three games. They have homered once in their last 55 innings. They are teetering. Bullpen game on national TV tomorrow night during a nor’easter.”
Phillies Star Schwarber Makes Statement
After the tough loss, Kyle Schwarber met with the media (h/t NBC Sports Philadelphia).
Reporter: “Kyle, we’ve heard you talk about… Just pressing on and playing tomorrow and all. Is it becoming harder and harder because of just the way things have gone the last few days?”
Schwarber: “No. I think that it’s what we got to do. There’s no ifs, ands, or buts about it. You move on to tomorrow. You have to find a way to win a game tomorrow. Keep trying to find a way to win games. We got two left. Still got the ball in our court right now. And if we go out there and we do what we need to do, we control our own future, and that’s what we want. I wouldn’t want it any other way than for us to decide what happens. So we move on to tomorrow.”
Looking At Schwarber
Schwarber is in the middle of his 12th season at the MLB level (and fifth with the Phillies).
Before his time with Philadelphia, the 2016 World Series Champion had stops with the Chicago Cubs, Washington Nationals and Boston Red Sox.
Right now, Schwarber is batting .233 with 133 hits, 45 home runs, 95 RBIs, 94 runs and three stolen bases in 153 games.
Looking At The Phillies Right Now
The Phillies are the second-place team in the National League East with an 87-73 record in 160 games.
They have gone 4-6 over their last ten games (and are 42-37 in 79 games at home).
Scott Lauber of The Philadelphia Inquirer wrote: “A 6.5-game lead over the Diamondbacks three weeks ago is down to one game with two to play. The Phillies can’t score runs or hold a lead. And they don’t have a starting pitcher for tonight. The metaphor is too obvious. It’s also unavoidable. The storm is here.”

item.content:encoded:
Soto was removed from Saturday's game against the Nationals after getting hit on the hand by a pitch, Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reports.
Soto was taken out of the game immediately after taking a 91.7-mph sinker off his right hand in the ninth inning. The Mets will likely send him in for imaging and should provide an update on his status in the near future, but with just one game left in the season and the Mets out of the playoff picture, he may sit out New York's season finale if he's still feeling sore Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
It hasn't been the 2026 campaign Vladimir Guerrero Jr. or the Toronto Blue Jays have hoped for by any stretch this season.
Toronto reached the World Series less than a year ago and came just inches away from winning it, but the Blue Jays will miss the postseason this year.
On Saturday, they'll play their second-to-last game of the regular season as they come off a 6-5 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Friday night in their series opener.
Ahead of Game 2 of the weekend set, Blue Jays manager John Schneider announced a notable lineup change involving Guerrero Jr.
Blue Jays Announce Guerrero Jr. Decision
After starting at first base on Friday and recording one hit and an RBI, Guerrero Jr. is back in the lineup again but will transition to designated hitter while batting third in the order, behind Brett Bateman, who returns to the lineup, and Nathan Lukes.
Here's the full Blue Jays lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Blue Jays 9/26 B. Bateman CF N. Lukes RF V. Guerrero Jr. DH A. Kirk C K. Okamoto 3B S. Keys 1B J. Smith LF A. Giménez SS E. Clement 2B T. Yesavage SP."
Guerrero Jr.'s 2026 Season
While the Blue Jays star was once again named an All-Star for the sixth straight year, he simply lacked power this season.
He's appeared in 142 games for Toronto in 2026 and, across 533 at-bats, he's hitting .263 with 71 runs, 140 hits, nine home runs, and 56 RBIs while slugging just .360 with a .695 OPS.
Guerrero Jr. made it very clear over the last few days that he plans on living up to the massive 14-year, $500 million contract he signed in 2025 after stirring up some controversy with comments earlier in the week.
He has since apologized for saying the Blue Jays paid him for what he's already accomplished, not what he's going to do in the future, and has retracted those statements.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Toronto Blue Jays Announce Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Decision During Reds Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] The devil in the details of Julio Rodríguez’s 2026 season
item.dc:creator: Kate Preusser
item.description: Julio Rodríguez has a new favorite phrase in English, one he said a couple of times at a pregame media availability on Friday: the devil's in the details.
